meta.note: Rule rows (PWC25 shape): id, world, statement (paraphrased), locators, speaker, mechanism, seam (AB code), derives (blocked slugs a playable model exists for), default_dial_reason, licence. Proposals: a batched reader (gpt-6-luna) read the books in shards of about 8,000 words; nothing here was human-checked, and no source text is kept. Commercial book: design reference only.

rules.statement: A power groups related effects under one source of energy and a defined focus, such as a kind of matter, phenomenon, target class, or abstract idea; source and focus may differ, and either may be shared across multiple powers.
locators: GURPS Powers: What Is a Power? (pp. 7–8) (gurps-powers#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a stated source and focus; dial: allow multiple or mismatched sources and focuses when the setting’s explanation supports them.

rules.statement: A power is made up of abilities, a power modifier, and a Talent. An advantage counts as one of the power’s abilities only if it has that power’s modifier, and it then follows the power’s special rules.
locators: GURPS Powers: Anatomy of a Power / Power Modifiers (pp. 7–8) (gurps-powers#000)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: bind each ability to its power through its modifier; dial: permit exceptions only if the campaign wants abilities that escape the power’s shared rules.

rules.statement: A power’s allowed abilities should fit its focus and generally work in related ways; the GM may restrict or qualify an ability to keep it within that focus, but may approve reasonable additions beyond the listed abilities.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: block effects that do not fit the focus; dial: broaden the permitted set when the fiction gives a coherent reason.

rules.statement: A power modifier makes an advantage subject to the power’s countermeasures, circumstances, or action restrictions; it is a limitation when these constrain the ability and an enhancement when they make it more flexible than the unmodified trait.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply the modifier’s restrictions or flexibility to every bound ability; dial: vary how severe they are according to the power’s circumstances and countermeasures.

rules.statement: A power’s Talent adds its level to all success rolls for activating or using any of its abilities, including IQ, Will, or Perception rolls where relevant. Talent normally costs 5 points per level, and a character may not buy above level 4 without GM permission.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: grant a shared bonus up to level 4; dial: allow higher aptitude only with GM approval, reflecting exceptional mastery.

rules.statement: A character may have a power’s abilities without its Talent, or its Talent without abilities; either way, the missing component can be added later.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow the power’s components to be acquired separately; dial: require them together if powers in the setting are inseparable.

rules.statement: An advantage counts as part of a power only when it has that power’s modifier. Effects that negate, drain, or enhance the power do not affect an unmodified version of the same advantage; effects that affect the unmodified version also affect modified versions.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: distinguish modified abilities from standalone traits; dial: allow the GM to restrict unusual traits to powers so their modifiers govern them.

rules.statement: A power’s abilities must fit both its focus and its source. Environmental limits can make an otherwise unsuitable ability fit—for example, restricting a binding effect to death-associated locations.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require abilities to make sense for the power; dial: permit creative exceptions when a limitation explains them.

rules.statement: If a power includes an ability that interferes with every power from a particular source, it generally cannot also include abilities from that source, except for Neutralize, Obscure, and Resistant.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an anti-source ability excludes ordinary abilities from that source; dial: allow the listed exceptions.

rules.statement: Several abilities may be treated as alternative settings of one trait: the most expensive costs full price and each other setting costs one-fifth of its final modified cost, rounded up. Only one setting works at a time; switching requires a Ready maneuver, and the settings cannot be linked.
locators: GURPS Powers: Optional Rule: Alternative Abilities, p. 11 (gurps-powers#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charge full price for every ability; dial: grant the one-fifth pricing when the GM approves the abilities as compatible settings.

rules.statement: Disabling, crippling, burning out, neutralizing, or draining any alternative setting disables the whole collection until that setting recovers. If an ability cannot be used again until its duration ends, the whole collection is unavailable for that duration.
locators: GURPS Powers: Optional Rule: Alternative Abilities, p. 11 (gurps-powers#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failure or lockout affects the entire collection; dial: use the reduced cost only if this shared vulnerability is accepted.

rules.statement: A power may provide bonuses to ST, DX, IQ, HT, Will, Perception, Basic Speed, or Basic Move only when the bonus requires conscious activation or does not always work, or when the power modifier itself genuinely limits it. The user declares when using the bonus; Talent does not improve it.
locators: GURPS Powers: Attributes as Abilities, p. 13 (gurps-powers#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: do not treat attribute bonuses as power abilities; dial: allow them when activation or the modifier limits their availability.

rules.statement: To transform someone other than the user, the power needs an Affliction with an Advantage enhancement appropriate to the transformation. Such an effect may accompany or replace the user’s own transformation ability.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transformations affect only the user; dial: allow effects on others by adding an appropriately enhanced Affliction.

rules.statement: Damage Resistance used to divert attacks should be limited to the power’s source or focus; for limitation pricing, a whole source counts as Very Common (-20%), while a single focus broad enough to justify a power counts as Common (-40%).
locators: GURPS Powers: Typical Defensive Abilities, p. 13 (gurps-powers#001)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: defenses are limited to the relevant source or focus; dial: choose broader or narrower protection, with the stated limitation values.

rules.statement: A power’s modifier is the sum of its individual enhancements and limitations; an ability bearing that modifier becomes part of the power. A modifier worth +0% marks a source without changing the ability’s ordinary play effects.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: source-only association is +0%; dial: add restrictions or broaden effects when the power’s source makes that appropriate.

rules.statement: A limitation is available when a power has a weakness its ordinary version would not have. Ordinary, commonly available environmental conditions or everyday objects that substantially hinder or stop it give -10%; don’t also discount an individual ability for the same weakness.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary built-in weaknesses remain unchanged; dial: use -10% when common environments or mundane means create an extra, exploitable failure point.

rules.statement: Specific unusual advantages or skills that can suppress a power give it -5%; widely usable specialized technology that does so also gives -5%. If both kinds apply, the total is -10%, cumulative with the mundane-countermeasure limitation.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no extra discount for ordinary counters; dial: apply -5% per applicable class, to reflect deliberate anti-power tools or capabilities.

rules.statement: If only the ordinary counters that affect an ability’s unpowered version apply, the countermeasure component is +0%. A cosmic power costs +50% and ignores ordinary counters, cannot be neutralized or cut off from its source, and works across worlds and bodies; only cosmic opposition can stop it.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary countermeasure exposure is +0%; dial: +50% for exceptional immunity, which requires similarly cosmic opposition to overcome.

rules.statement: When a power requires a code of conduct, violating it removes all of the user’s abilities. The required disadvantages normally total -5 to -15 points and contribute the same amount as a percentage limitation; add +5% if the power fades gradually, use +0% if it vanishes quickly, and subtract -5% if it turns against the user.
locators: GURPS Powers: Required Behavior and Power Modifier, pp. 23-24 (gurps-powers#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: violations suspend the whole power; dial: the code’s burden and the speed or hostility of enforcement set the discount.

rules.statement: Restoring a lost power gives +5% if a day’s downtime or income sacrifice suffices; use +0% for a week, a minor quest, or minor harm, and -5% for a month, a major quest, or serious harm. Add this to the conduct and enforcement adjustments, but any positive final adjustment is reduced to +0%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Required Behavior and Power Modifier, pp. 23-24 (gurps-powers#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restoration difficulty is part of the power’s total modifier; dial: easier amends reduce the discount, while costly recovery increases it.

rules.statement: A power that uses external ambient energy gets +0% if the energy cannot be screened or drained, -5% if only esoteric or supernatural means can cut it off, and -10% if mundane insulation can block it. Use only one of these values for a given shortcoming.
locators: GURPS Powers: Channeled Energies: Ambient Energies, p. 25 (gurps-powers#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: internal energy sources do not qualify; dial: the degree to which the external source can be cut off determines the limitation.

rules.statement: A power that petitions willful intermediaries requires a reaction roll each time the user tries to use an ability; ordinary reaction modifiers and Talent do not affect that roll, though the GM may apply situational modifiers. This fickle arrangement is worth -20%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Channeled Energies: Fickle Forces, p. 25 (gurps-powers#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no fickleness unless the source can refuse; dial: a -20% discount buys uncertain access whenever an ability is invoked.

rules.statement: An ability’s use can cost fatigue at -5% per FP per use; if the FP must come from an Energy Reserve, add another -5% because an empty reserve prevents use. A continuing effect follows its separate cost rules.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use has no added fatigue cost; dial: charge FP and further limit access when only a dedicated reserve can pay.

rules.statement: When several powers share an ability, the user must choose which power supplies it and apply only that power’s modifier; modifiers from different powers do not apply together. An ability cannot carry multiple power modifiers, except that a power may be both Elemental and Super.
locators: GURPS Powers: Stacking Power Modifiers, p. 28 (gurps-powers#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one source modifier governs each purchase; dial: the stated exception allows the two named source categories to coexist.

rules.statement: Talent adds its level to the user’s success rolls for abilities assigned to that one power, but not to damage, resistance, or other effect rolls, nor normally to reaction rolls or rolls to overcome an ability limitation. A roll cannot benefit from more than one power’s Talent; four levels is suggested as a usual ceiling, and levels cost 5, 10, or 15 points depending on breadth.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply Talent only to the user’s ability-use success rolls; dial its maximum and price by scope to prevent broad powers from overwhelming ordinary attributes and skills.

rules.statement: When two powers oppose one another, their abilities may block or parry each other without either removing the other’s users’ powers; a true anti-power instead needs abilities such as Neutralize and Static against the powers it counters. A one-way anti-power should have only anti-abilities and a modifier of at least +0%, while two-way counters must include the -5% anti-power discount.
locators: GURPS Powers: pp. 31–32, Power vs. Power; p. 33, One-Way / Two-Way (gurps-powers#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: specify the counters in the power descriptions; dial whether opposition merely blocks effects or can suppress abilities, because stronger counters sharply constrain the targeted powers.

rules.statement: Powers may be arranged in tiers so that a higher-tier ability treats a lower-tier one as if it were cosmic when they interact, while lower tiers cannot overcome higher ones. In systems with two through six tiers, the tier premium ranges from +0% at the lowest tier to +50% at the highest; lingering attacks add the basic tier premium, and attacks that ignore lesser powers add five times that premium.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 32, Powers, Great and Small (gurps-powers#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary traits interact regardless of source; dial tiers and premiums to represent a hierarchy, paying more for effects that endure or penetrate defenses.

rules.statement: The GM can restrict which abilities belong to a power: prerequisites can require earlier abilities or a minimum Talent; secret abilities may require proof, a Talent threshold, or research; and level limits cap expenditure or scale with Talent. Required modifiers can also raise an ability’s cost or impose a control limitation.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 31, Structure Within Powers (gurps-powers#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: these restrictions do not reduce the power’s cost; dial prerequisites, secrecy, caps, and modifiers to prevent abuse and give the power a structured progression.

rules.statement: A potential ability costs half its usual modified price but cannot function until its owner spends earned points to pay the remaining cost. The GM may require only the points, a suitable trigger, or training before activation.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a potential ability is inert until fully paid for; dial activation conditions to make hidden capabilities emerge through immediate payment, an ordeal, or instruction.

rules.statement: A character may improve an existing power only after relevant use: adding Talent or improving an ability requires use in the previous session or adventure, while a new ability also requires a suitable trigger and its prerequisites. Per session, allow only one improvement, such as one Talent level, one ability level, one modifier change, or one new ability; a new ability may have to carry a control limitation for at least one session, and a power modifier cannot be changed.
locators: GURPS Powers: pp. 34–35, Improving Existing Powers (gurps-powers#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require recent use and limit advancement to one change per session; dial triggers and temporary drawbacks to tie growth to experience and keep powers from expanding too quickly.

rules.statement: Training can grant one point of Talent or ability per 200 hours, or instead allow a student who has enough earned points to buy a teacher-known improvement after sufficient instruction. A GM may make training mandatory or optional, and Talent may reduce learning time by 10% per level.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: instruction is campaign-dependent; dial whether it supplies points or merely access, and whether it is required, to make learning fit the power’s tradition and pace.

rules.statement: A trigger may be required in addition to points to awaken an ability or power; triggers can include deliberate intervention, practice, danger, or exposure. The GM may call for a HT roll for physical abilities or Will for mental ones; Talent modifies it, as do bonuses of +5 for a potential ability, +0 for another ability in an already-awakened power, -5 for a first ability when the subject has only Talent, and -10 for a wholly new power.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a trigger may be required in addition to points; dial its strength and penalties to make awakening a consequence of circumstance, effort, or risk.

rules.statement: When a new power is gained, it may arrive fully usable, with control limitations, as potential abilities, or as Talent alone; the GM decides which. The character may have to pay the full price immediately, put all earned points toward a debt, receive it as a free award, or accept disadvantages as its cost.
locators: GURPS Powers: pp. 36–37, Adding New Powers; p. 37, Paying the Price (gurps-powers#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: define what is granted and how its cost is met; dial immediate payment, debt, gift, or drawbacks to reflect the source and consequences of empowerment.

rules.statement: The GM can limit which sources and foci players may choose, exclude abilities, set level limits or required modifiers, and restrict each power’s scope. Powers may be assigned to player characters or reserved for non-player characters, with no mechanical distinction between those categories.
locators: GURPS Powers: pp. 33–34, PC Powers vs. NPC Powers; p. 37, Player-Designed Powers (gurps-powers#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the GM determines access and may veto unsuitable designs; dial allowed sources, abilities, and scope to preserve the campaign’s intended setting and balance.

rules.statement: Custom power modifiers should generally be kept between -10% and -20%; even a 0% limitation can support distinctive effects.
locators: GURPS Powers: Page 39, preceding Chapter Two (gurps-powers#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: An ability is built from one or more underlying advantages, optional modifiers, optional special effects, and a name. Special effects may change gameplay but do not change point cost.
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: When an Affliction is unquestionably beneficial, the GM may reverse the sign of its HT modifier; its duration is minutes equal to the subject’s success margin rather than failure margin. With Malediction, a willing subject may forgo resistance, and duration is minutes equal to the user’s success margin.
locators: GURPS Powers: Page 40, Optional Rules for Afflictions (gurps-powers#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: An Affliction can affect a target with a HT score only if that target is susceptible to its effect. Most machines and other inanimate objects resist metabolic effects; an effect restricted to a suitable kind of inanimate target can affect it instead, while transformation effects can affect inanimate targets subject to an added size-based resistance that becomes automatic at modified HT 21 or more.
locators: GURPS Powers: Page 40, Afflictions and Inanimate Targets (gurps-powers#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: If an Affliction has a secondary effect that applies only when the target fails its HT roll by 5 or more, or critically fails, that effect is worth one-fifth as much as a primary effect. The GM may also treat effects requiring a critical success on the user’s roll as secondary.
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: When Summonable Allies produce new beings on each use, the GM makes a reaction roll to determine whether they will obey; the GM may also require Minion. If summoned beings are killed, replacements cannot be called for a full day.
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: A projection leaves its physical body unconscious, not suspended from bodily needs or harm; the body still requires food, water, air, and sleep, and can be affected by injury or fatigue. HP and FP losses are shared between body and projection, and negative conditions also affect the projection.
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: If a projection would become unconscious, it vanishes and the mind returns to the body, which stays unconscious until it recovers. If the projection dies, the projector’s mind and personality are lost; if the body dies, a Will-15 roll, modified by Talent, determines whether the projector becomes an Astral Entity or dies.
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: With the Construct enhancement, a projected duplicate that is dispelled leaves its creator at their current HP and FP, and its death is not permanent: the creator can spend 10 FP and take a Concentrate maneuver to create a replacement. If the original dies, all duplicates die as well.
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: Sequential duplicates are numbered from the original upward; if one dies, every higher-numbered duplicate vanishes. Adding Construct allows dead duplicates to be replaced by copies from other possible futures.
rules.speaker: rulebook

rules.statement: Appearance alteration can be either a real change to the body’s surface or an illusion that only looks real; decide which when acquiring the ability, with no difference in point cost.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the user can alter appearance; dial: real change versus illusion; the in-world reason is whether the body itself changes.

rules.statement: Remote empathy can read a subject’s emotions and general motivations when the user can see or hear them, including through electronic media or supernatural means where applicable; it costs +50%.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 48, Empathy Advantages — New Special Enhancement (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: empathy requires direct personal contact; dial: remote access costs +50%; the reason is that mediated perception extends the ability’s reach.

rules.statement: Enhanced Move can be limited to a subset of its normal environment, but the restriction must genuinely narrow that environment—for example, movement among trees or tall buildings can qualify where simply requiring air would not.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 48, Enhanced Move — New Special Limitations (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: movement applies in its usual environment; dial: a valid environmental restriction narrows where it works; the in-world condition is the specific terrain.

rules.statement: With the All-Out limitation, using Enhanced Move leaves the user without active defenses and unable to attack, concentrate, ready items, or take similar actions while moving fast; it costs -20%.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 48, Enhanced Move — New Special Limitations (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: movement does not impose these action restrictions; dial: All-Out costs -20%; the in-world reason is that full attention is occupied by moving.

rules.statement: Enhanced Tracking can let a user keep multiple targets tracked even with only one weapon, and retain the benefit of Aim or Evaluate when attacking any tracked target; it costs +20%.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 49, Enhanced Tracking — New Special Enhancement (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: tracking multiple targets does not itself grant this weapon-use benefit; dial: the enhancement costs +20%; the in-world capability is maintaining several target locks.

rules.statement: Extra Attack can be enhanced to let the user strike repeatedly with the same weapon or body part, including making more attacks than available limbs or attack abilities would normally allow; it costs +20%.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 49, Extra Attack — New Special Enhancement (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attacks are bounded by available limbs, weapons, and attack abilities; dial: repeated use of the same attack costs +20%; the in-world explanation is exceptional attack output.

rules.statement: Flight with Requires Surface can remain airborne for no more than five seconds, then the user must touch a rigid surface—or, in a cinematic game, any surface—to push off again, without spending a maneuver; otherwise the user falls. The limitation is worth -20%.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 50, Flight — New Special Limitations (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: flight does not require periodic contact; dial: this version limits airtime to five seconds and costs -20%; the in-world cause is needing a surface to push against.

rules.statement: A Healing ability with Cure Affliction can neutralize ongoing Afflictions and similar effects from Side Effect or Symptoms. The user rolls IQ at -1 for each full +50% of the target effect’s enhancement value and spends twice the penalty in FP, minimum 1 FP; for example, a +50% effect takes a -1 roll and 2 FP. The enhancement costs +60%.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 51, Healing — New Special Enhancements (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Healing does not remove these ongoing effects; dial: this treatment costs +60%, with a penalty and FP cost scaling to the effect; the in-world burden reflects the severity of what is being undone.

rules.statement: With Empathic Healing, removing injuries, diseases, or Afflictions from another person transfers them to the healer instead of costing FP; the transferred conditions affect the healer even if normally immune, and improve at the usual natural rate unless treated. This limitation is worth -50% and cannot be combined with Capped.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 51, Healing — New Special Limitations (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: healing does not transfer the target’s conditions to the user; dial: Empathic is worth -50% and excludes Capped; the in-world cost is personally bearing what was removed.

rules.statement: A severed body part can be reattached by holding it in place for one minute; a temporarily or lastingly crippled part can be reattached but remains crippled, while a permanently crippled part is destroyed.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 52, Independent Body Parts (gurps-powers#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: severed parts are not automatically restored; dial: reattachment requires a minute and cannot restore a permanently crippled part; the in-world limitation is the part’s damage state.

rules.statement: A character with Jumper (Spirit) spends 1 FP per attempt and rolls IQ to shift between realms. Failure leaves the character where they are and imposes -5 on attempts to use the ability again for 10 minutes; critical-failure results are set by the GM.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: realm travel is not automatic; dial: each attempt costs 1 FP and failure temporarily penalizes reuse; the in-world risk is instability or other mishap during the crossing.

rules.statement: Jumper (Time) or (World) models travel through time or between worlds; Projection can adapt other Jumper forms to spirit travel, and Interplanar can extend spirit travel to divine realms. Talent adds to the IQ roll to activate any Jumper.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel is limited to the relevant kind of destination; dial: choose time, world, or spirit access, with Projection or Interplanar broadening the route.

rules.statement: Super-Effort replaces the ordinary extra-effort procedure for a Lifting ST lift: use the Size and Speed/Range table to convert the Lifting ST level into a ST bonus. Each such lift costs 1 FP, with further exertion costing 1 FP per minute for walking with or pulling the load, or 1 FP per hour for merely holding it; this never boosts grapples or chokes. Reduced Fatigue Cost cannot remove these costs without Cosmic, and the enhancement costs +400%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Lifting ST — New Special Enhancement (gurps-powers#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: extraordinary lifting consumes fatigue; dial: Cosmic can remove the reduced-cost restriction, but only at an additional +50%.

rules.statement: Wishing lets the user request two rerolls for any die roll made in the character’s presence, including another person’s roll, and choose the preferred result. The character must witness the event, and ordinary Luck usage limits still apply; the enhancement costs +100%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Luck — New Special Enhancement (gurps-powers#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: Luck is not necessarily consciously controlled; dial: Wishing enables deliberate probability influence but requires witnessing the roll and retains normal use limits.

rules.statement: Discriminatory Mana Damper or Mana Enhancer gives allies in the area the most favorable mana level the ability can produce, while enemies there receive the least favorable one. It includes Switchable and replaces Selective Area, and costs +150%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Mana Damper and Mana Enhancer — New Special Enhancement (gurps-powers#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mana changes affect the area without distinguishing sides; dial: this version favors allies and hinders enemies, at a higher enhancement cost.

rules.statement: Medium senses and permits speech with nearby unbound spirits, including spirits of a place only while the user is within their inhabited area; it does not cover living spirits or spirits bound to objects. Each variant for communicating with another kind of otherworldly resident is a separate ability.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: communication is limited to nearby, unbound spirits; dial: alternate spirit-like populations require separate versions, and séance use may require preparation.

rules.statement: Mastery permits instant, precise metabolic adjustments; while conscious, the user adds their Metabolism Control level to any HT roll. It costs +40%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Metabolism Control — New Special Enhancement (gurps-powers#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary Metabolism Control has narrower applications; dial: Mastery extends its benefit to any HT roll, but only while conscious.

rules.statement: Independent Mind Control requires concentration to begin, but after a failed resistance attempt the user can turn to other activities. Control lasts one minute per point by which the victim lost the Quick Contest; it cannot be extended indefinitely by concentration, and only a demand contrary to the victim’s principles breaks it. Each victim is handled separately, with no accumulating penalty per slave, and a critical failure against one does not free the others; the enhancement costs +70%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Mind Control — New Special Enhancement (gurps-powers#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control normally demands continuing attention; dial: Independent frees attention and separates victims’ outcomes, but imposes a fixed duration and a principle-based escape condition.

rules.statement: Multiple Contacts allows Mind Reading to keep channels open to several minds, at a cumulative -1 per contact beyond the first. The user can switch among established channels without another roll but can read only one mind at a time, choosing the target each combat turn; it costs +50%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Mind Probe and Mind Reading — New Special Enhancements (gurps-powers#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one channel at a time; dial: multiple channels can remain established, at a growing penalty and with focused reading still limited to one mind.

rules.statement: Modular Abilities can reassign their points among eligible traits; the point cost per slot depends on breadth, from 4 points for a short list to 7 for anything, while each ability point costs 2–5 points depending on whether rearrangement is slow, costly, or vulnerable to interference. In the example, nearly any ability costs 6 points per slot plus 4 per point, and changing it takes at least one second of prayer per character point, with the deity sometimes overruling the request.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: broad reconfiguration is expensive; dial: lower costs require slower, costlier, or interruptible changes, while divine intervention can override a requested configuration.

rules.statement: Obscure normally creates a detectable field or cloud that impedes signals crossing it in both directions; the affected senses determine what it blocks, and penalties also affect matching telecommunications when a sender or receiver is inside the area. A Stealthy version conceals both user and field; supernatural versions commonly avoid hindering the user and add Defensive, while an ultra-tech version generally disrupts the user’s sensors too.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect blocks signals across its area in both directions and is detectable; dial: Stealthy concealment and Defensive protection reduce those drawbacks, while technology may impair its own user.

rules.statement: Meld 1 lets the user merge with a discrete object they can permeate, sense from it, and exit from any point on its interior or exterior surface with a Ready maneuver; breathing is possible if any part touches air. Damage to the object harms the user in proportion to their respective hit points, the object’s greater size improves resistance to afflictions, and the user cannot control the object; the enhancement costs +150%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Permeation — New Special Enhancements (gurps-powers#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passing through material does not itself grant merging; dial: Meld adds concealment and exit access but makes the user share proportional damage with the object.

rules.statement: Precognition requires the GM to establish how often visions occur, how far ahead they can reach, and whether the future can change; visions should generally remain vague and, except on a critical success, do not provide hard facts such as winning numbers. The future should retain some inevitable truth, especially around a Destiny.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: visions offer uncertain, incomplete warning; dial: the GM sets frequency, horizon, and mutability, while vague details and an inevitable kernel limit the information.

rules.statement: With Directed, the user names a future event before rolling; success reveals its most likely outcome, failure reveals nothing, and a critical failure permanently prevents future visions of that event. This option cannot be combined with One Event and adds +100%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: general visions; dial: focus on a named event for +100%; the risk is losing all future visions of it on a critical failure.

rules.statement: With Directed, the user states which past event to investigate before rolling; success yields relevant information, failure yields nothing, and a critical failure permanently blocks access to that part of history. It adds +50%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: receive general impressions; dial: target a particular past event for +50%; a critical failure closes that history to the user forever.

rules.statement: With Immersive, a successful reading replays emotionally charged events: at a place, the user sees and hears events as if present, while reading an object shows events from its point of view. It adds +100%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: receive impressions rather than a replay; dial: experience a vivid sensory reconstruction for +100%; the risk is that it can give away mysteries too easily.

rules.statement: With Hypersensory, the user infers the past from subtle physical clues and takes a -3 penalty if unable to use one of smell, touch, or vision, or -6 if unable to use two. The ability fails if all three are blocked or the GM judges there are no clues; this option includes Mundane and cannot be combined with Immersive or Sensitive.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: psychic impressions; dial: infer history from sensory evidence; access to clues and usable senses limits what can be learned.

rules.statement: The broader the ancestral group whose memories can be accessed, the less specific those memories are; this does not change the ability’s point cost. With Immersive, a successful reading replays ancestral memories, and passive visions need no interpretation; active use can replay ancestors’ lives at will. It adds +50%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: broader access gives vaguer memories; dial: add an immersive replay for +50%; the breadth of ancestry trades detail for reach.

rules.statement: Protected Power gives a power +5 to resist Neutralize attempts and +5 when using it to break through Static with the Resistible limitation; it does not protect the power’s sensory abilities. It costs 5 points per power.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the power has no special resistance; dial: pay 5 points per power for +5 resistance against direct disruption, without shielding its senses.

rules.statement: With Words of Power, the user can affect opponents regardless of language and can affect those normally immune to being fazed. Each use is a Quick Contest of Will; ordinary penalties apply when targeting a group, while modifiers for Clueless and No Sense of Humor are ignored. It adds +100%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: verbal provocation follows ordinary limits; dial: supernatural words bypass language and certain immunities for +100%; group use remains harder.

rules.statement: With Reattachment, the user can restore any severed, intact body part by holding it in place for one minute. Regeneration shortens this to 30 seconds if Slow, three seconds if Regular, or one second if Fast or better; this option adds +50%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a lost part must regrow; dial: reattach an intact part for +50%; it must be recovered and held in place, though Regeneration can shorten the wait.

rules.statement: With Active Change, transformation takes its usual amount of time but does not require concentration, so the user can move and act during it. The user retains the abilities of the form they are leaving until the change is complete; this adds +20%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: changing form occupies the user; dial: allow movement and action during the usual transition for +20%; the new form’s abilities wait until completion.

rules.statement: Recall retrieves only the user’s personal possessions across space or dimensions; it takes 10 seconds, costs 2 FP, and requires an IQ roll, with no penalties. Retrieved items remain indefinitely and can be sent back at any time; this option cannot be combined with Creation, Permanent, or Unpredictable, and gives -25%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retrieved items are subject to the ability’s ordinary use; dial: restrict retrieval to personal possessions for -25%; retrieval still costs time, fatigue, and a successful roll.

rules.statement: A force-field extension works like ordinary limb extension, but the projected part cannot be injured. The user must move the corresponding limbs, needs a free hand to pick up or wield something, and is limited to natural ST and DX; it cannot pass through barriers or perform actions a real limb could not.
locators: GURPS Powers: Stretching — New Special Enhancement, p. 78 (gurps-powers#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the extension remains constrained by the user’s real limbs and abilities; dial: allow sturdier projected extensions, at the cost of changing those limits.

rules.statement: A character with both extreme flexibility and limb extension can squeeze through narrow openings by reducing effective size modifier in one or two dimensions by the extension level.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the reduction applies in only one or two dimensions; dial: permit greater compression, at the cost of making passage through tight spaces easier.

rules.statement: A rebound enhancement lets the user roll against the best of DX, Acrobatics, or Jumping after a fall or collision. Apply -5 for each multiple, or fraction, by which velocity exceeds jumping Move; success prevents damage and rebounds at 90% of impact velocity, while failure causes normal damage and ends the rebound.
locators: GURPS Powers: Super Jump — New Special Enhancements, p. 81 (gurps-powers#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rebounds preserve only 90% of impact velocity and faster impacts penalize the roll; dial: soften those limits, at the cost of making collisions less dangerous.

rules.statement: A midair-control enhancement lets the jumper steer as though using Flight, with air Move equal to jumping Move; calculate jump distance and hang time normally. It cannot be combined with the listed special limitations except the planetary limitation.
locators: GURPS Powers: Super Jump — New Special Enhancements, p. 81 (gurps-powers#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: steering is restricted by the listed incompatibilities and the jump’s normal hang time; dial: allow combinations or longer control, at the cost of greater aerial mobility.

rules.statement: With retroactive luck, the user may declare immediately after a roll that its result was different, changing the past. Once anyone makes another roll, the user can no longer alter that event; the change is visibly apparent.
locators: GURPS Powers: Super Luck — New Special Enhancements, p. 80 (gurps-powers#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: alteration must be declared before another roll and leaves visible evidence; dial: widen the window or hide the change, at the cost of weakening those constraints.

rules.statement: A high-speed transmission enhancement sends information at 10, 100, 1,000, or more times normal speed for +30%, +60%, +90%, and so on; each tenfold increase gives intercept attempts a -1 penalty. It is unavailable for directional-sound and sonar communication.
locators: GURPS Powers: Telecommunication — New Special Enhancements, p. 82 (gurps-powers#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: greater speed makes interception harder only by one penalty step per tenfold increase; dial: increase speed or interception difficulty, at the cost of making signals harder to monitor.

rules.statement: A secure transmission makes an interceptor win a Quick Contest of IQ when using the ability, or Electronics Operation when using equipment, against the sender’s IQ to understand it; a loser receives meaningless content. The enhancement costs +20%.
locators: GURPS Powers: Telecommunication — New Special Enhancements, p. 83 (gurps-powers#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: security depends on a contest and a losing interceptor gets garbage; dial: strengthen or weaken the security, at the cost of making interception respectively harder or easier.

rules.statement: When telekinesis affects multiple targets in combat, it must affect them in the same way; roll separately for each target, at a penalty equal to the number of targets minus one. For collective uses, use total affected weight to determine encumbrance from telekinetic Basic Lift, and move affected objects at telekinetic level reduced by encumbrance.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each additional combat target worsens the roll and combined weight reduces movement; dial: ease either limit, at the cost of broader or stronger group control.

rules.statement: Animated objects need telekinetic level at least equal to their HP if unliving or half their HP if homogeneous. They use the user’s DX and their animation-level telekinetic ST; their Move is telekinetic level minus the level needed to animate them, and they return to rest when control ends.
locators: GURPS Powers: Telekinesis — New Special Limitations, p. 84 (gurps-powers#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: object durability sets the power threshold, movement uses up available level, and motion stops when control ends; dial: loosen these limits, at the cost of more capable or persistent animated objects.

rules.statement: An attraction-only or repulsion-only telekinetic effect requires a Ready maneuver to move an unresisting object and an Attack maneuver against an active opponent. It cannot strike, manipulate, or pin targets; opposition to movement is resolved by a Quick Contest of ST or telekinetic level against the user’s telekinetic level.
locators: GURPS Powers: Telekinesis — New Special Limitations, p. 84 (gurps-powers#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect moves targets only along the toward-or-away axis and does not restrain or attack them; dial: expand its functions, at the cost of reducing the restriction that defines the effect.

rules.statement: After thinking about a task for a full minute, you can give a sapient being you can see or touch the ability’s usual success bonus on that task. Only one bonus can be pending at a time, for you or another person; you can cancel it to help with a different task.
locators: GURPS Powers: Visualization — New Special Enhancements (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one pending bonus; dial: the user can redirect it before the roll; reason: focused thought must be spent on a particular task.

rules.statement: After visualizing a visible or touchable victim failing at a task for a full minute, you can impose a penalty equal to your usual bonus when the victim attempts that task. Only one curse can be active at a time, it can be canceled to curse another task, and this ability cannot also provide a blessing or affect its user.
locators: GURPS Powers: Visualization — New Special Enhancements (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one active curse; dial: the user can cancel and redirect it; reason: sustained attention is devoted to one victim’s task.

rules.statement: A reflexive teleport can be attempted once per turn as a dodge: make an IQ roll without the usual preparation penalty, then appear in the first safe open space in a randomly determined direction. If no such space is within 10 yards, the teleport fails; this option cannot be combined with Hyperjump.
locators: GURPS Powers: Warp — New Special Enhancements (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one attempt per turn and random direction; dial: the GM may allow use in other dangerous situations; reason: fear and adrenaline trigger an uncontrolled escape.

rules.statement: With this limitation, every teleport lands at a random point within a circle whose radius is 1% of the traveled distance, with a minimum radius of 1 yard; a better IQ roll means a closer arrival. A critical failure can put the user high in the air or underground.
locators: GURPS Powers: Warp — New Special Limitations (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: arrival has a distance-scaled error; dial: the GM chooses the precise location; reason: imprecise teleportation trades accuracy for a cheaper ability.

rules.statement: To follow another teleporter, add a penalty of 1 per yard from your location to their departure point, and modify the roll for how long ago they left: from +10 if they just departed to -10 at eight hours, with a further -1 per doubling of time afterward. Success takes you to their arrival point; failure by 1 still follows them but causes the effects of drift.
locators: GURPS Powers: Warp — New Special Enhancements (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: distance and elapsed time make tracking harder; dial: the usual teleport modifiers still apply; reason: the trail fades and its destination must be reached by teleporting.

rules.statement: Control requires the relevant element to be present and never creates it; its target is limited by level and must be a single object or continuous area, except where Collective applies. Taking control of solids or liquids requires touching the target and winning an unarmed melee attack, followed by an IQ roll; gases, energy, or forces require entering the area, concentrating, and rolling IQ, while an already-controlled target requires winning a Quick Contest.
locators: GURPS Powers: Control — Limits of Control; Establishing Control (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: control needs an existing, bounded target and an establishment roll; dial: Collective can widen which instances are affected; reason: the user must first reach and overpower the element’s current control.

rules.statement: Once established, control can reshape a target with concentration; moving or flowing it also requires continuous concentration and proceeds at Move equal to the Control level. When concentration ends, stable forms remain, but unstable ones collapse immediately.
locators: GURPS Powers: Control — Effects of Control (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reshaping and movement demand concentration; dial: Persistent can maintain effects for 10 seconds after concentration stops; reason: the user’s attention sustains unstable changes.

rules.statement: Each attempt to create an element costs 2 FP, whether it succeeds or fails; created matter vanishes after 10 seconds unless stabilized. Stabilizing it spends points from a Creation Pool: each point preserves matter worth 10% of average starting wealth, and those points remain unavailable until the matter vanishes and they are reclaimed.
locators: GURPS Powers: Create — Limits on Quantity (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: matter is temporary and costly to preserve; dial: the GM may waive permanent-creation point costs if economics do not matter; reason: lasting matter ties up a limited creation reserve.

rules.statement: A created hazardous element can be used as a short-lived attack: for example, corrosive or poisonous solids and liquids inflict 1d damage per level once on one subject, while hazardous energy or fire inflicts 1 point per level each second to those in its area for up to 10 seconds. The substance or energy used for such attacks vanishes after producing its effect.
locators: GURPS Powers: Create — Limits on Quantity (gurps-powers#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attack quantities are limited by level and rapidly vanish; dial: the user chooses an eligible hazardous element before rolling; reason: brief, bounded creation prevents persistent hazards.

rules.statement: An illusion is maintained by concentration and can deceive observers who lose an IQ-versus-Perception Quick Contest; when someone already fooled changes how they interact with it, resolve a new contest. An observer gets +4 if warned or if the creator critically fails against someone else, and +10 for an obvious illusion or examination using a sense the illusion cannot fool.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: deception depends on each observer’s contest and continued concentration; dial: additional senses can be fooled with enhancements; reason: scrutiny and warning expose the illusion’s flaws.

rules.statement: Independent illusions act without concentration and can converse and move within the effect area as if they had your DX, IQ, and skills. They behave like completely loyal, insubstantial NPCs, but have no thoughts and cannot perform tasks for you; they only react to their surroundings.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep the figures reactive rather than independently thinking; dial their mobility and apparent agency to fit the desired illusion.

rules.statement: A mental illusion requires a Concentrate maneuver and a Quick Contest of your IQ against the target’s Will; take -1 for each person already affected. On a win, you control that target’s sensory impressions, but not their thoughts, and the illusion cannot physically injure them; if they cannot see the real world, they act at -10 but can still act.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sensory control is limited to one target’s perceptions at a time and leaves their thoughts and ability to act intact; dial wider only by accepting the penalties.

rules.statement: After first successfully imposing mental illusions, you may contest IQ against the target’s Will once per second; each victory inflicts actual injury equal to your margin of victory. If the target falls unconscious for any reason, including this injury, you can no longer harm them.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: injury requires an established illusion and repeated successful contests, and stops when the victim is unconscious.

rules.statement: While you maintain contact with a living victim, each Leech level drains 1 HP per second, and you recover 1 HP for each full 3 HP drained; you cannot heal above normal HP. The drain ends immediately if contact ends, the victim escapes, or the victim dies.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: continuous contact and a 3-to-1 drain-to-healing ratio limit the benefit; dial up drain rate by buying more levels.

rules.statement: Leech can instead drain ST, DX, IQ, HT, or FP at 1 point per level per second, stopping when the victim’s score reaches 0. Victims recover lost scores at their normal FP-recovery rate, and the user heals 1 HP per 3 points drained, subject to the applicable healing option.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: drained scores return at the victim’s FP-recovery rate and cannot be reduced below 0; dial which score is targeted and its cost.

rules.statement: Neutralize requires touching the subject and winning a Quick Contest of Will; the target adds their best relevant Talent to their resistance. Success suppresses powers from the specified source for minutes equal to your margin of victory, but does not remove Talent or abilities from other sources; a critical failure disables your ability for 1d hours.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: suppression is source-specific, resisted, and temporary; broader source coverage requires buying the ability separately for each source.

rules.statement: Static prevents powers from one specified source from directly affecting you or your carried or worn equipment, and it blocks friendly as well as hostile effects. It does not stop indirect attacks, and you cannot possess the powers or Talent of any source you negate.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protection covers direct effects on you and your equipment, not indirect hazards, and also blocks beneficial effects.

rules.statement: With Area Effect on a normally single-target, non-attack ability that costs FP, multiply its FP cost by the area’s radius in yards; one payment covers everyone in the area. If the ability uses a Quick Contest, contest separately against each potential victim, and apply any per-additional-victim penalty based on the total number of potential victims.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: area use scales FP cost by radius and requires separate contests; dial area size with the corresponding increase in cost and contest workload.

rules.statement: Static with Area Effect extends from the user, with the first level covering a 1-yard radius and each additional level doubling that radius. Discriminatory Static can spare friendly powers, while Switchable Static takes a Ready maneuver to turn on or off; Resisting it allows an attacker to break through with a Quick Contest of Will.
locators: GURPS Powers: Static — Special Enhancements and Limitation (gurps-powers#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: area protection grows exponentially by level; dial whether allies are affected, whether switching takes an action, and whether opponents can contest it.

rules.statement: When enhancements and limitations are combined, the default is to add their percentages before applying the total to the ability’s cost, and limitations cannot reduce cost by more than 80%. An optional method applies enhancements first and then limitations, with the same 80% maximum limitation reduction.
locators: GURPS Powers: Modifiers — Optional Rule: Multiplicative Modifiers (gurps-powers#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use additive modifiers and cap discounts at 80%; dial to multiplicative pricing only if the campaign prefers that treatment for large enhancements.

rules.statement: A target’s first defense against an overhead strike is at -2; later attacks assume the target is alert. A strike that swings around behind the target also gives -2 to defenses. In the special behind-the-target variant, most victims cannot actively defend; those with 360° or peripheral vision defend normally, while Danger Sense allows a Perception roll to defend at -2.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ordinary overhead or runaround attacks impose the stated defense penalties; dial: the special variant costs +150% and removes most active defenses because the attack begins behind the target.

rules.statement: A GM-approved pact can tie an ability to a genre-supporting vow; in the example, breaking the no-guns vow removes the character’s bullet protection for the remainder of that fight. A required disadvantage can likewise disable an ability if its needs are unmet, and the ability returns only after those needs are met and all resulting ill effects are fully recovered; price this restriction like a pact.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the agreement or required condition limits access to the ability; dial: the GM approves the pact and sets its genre fit, with lost protection or recovery from unmet needs as the cost.

rules.statement: An ability that innately affects an area need not have Area Effect to use Persistent. Successive attacks can leave it operating in several different areas at once unless its underlying trait prevents this, but repeated uses in one area do not accumulate.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: separate areas may remain active, but effects in the same area do not stack; dial: the underlying trait may forbid multiple areas, reflecting its limits.

rules.statement: A normally touch-only or zero-range ability may be allowed to work at a distance with Ranged, including certain information-gathering abilities. The user may still use it in its ordinary touch or surrounding-area mode, and Ranged is required before adding ranged-attack-statistic modifiers to an ability that normally has no range.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ability retains its usual mode and gains distance use; dial: the GM decides which abilities qualify, and ranged-attack-statistic modifiers require Ranged first.

rules.statement: For an ability whose FP cost is multiplied by another rule, Reduced Fatigue Cost subtracts 1 FP per level after that multiplication. For example, with area healing, multiply the cost by the radius first and then apply the reduction.
locators: GURPS Powers: Reduced Fatigue Cost, p. 106 (gurps-powers#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each level subtracts 1 FP after all cost multipliers; dial: the subtraction is capped by the resulting cost, so the ability cannot consume less than its remaining cost.

rules.statement: A sense-dependent ability fails if the user cannot access the required sense, including when that sense is blocked or when a technological or paranormal intermediary is used. This reversed sense restriction is available only for an advantage normally unaffected by DR and receives its usual limitation discount.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the ability requires direct access to the specified sense; dial: blocking that sense or relying on an intermediary prevents use.

rules.statement: An ability that requires concentration to control can become self-sustaining after an initial Concentrate or Ready maneuver. If it requires a roll, its duration is the margin of success in minutes, or its usual duration if shorter; it persists despite the user’s incapacitation or death, but the user cannot change or end it early, and it does not create extra instances unless the trait normally allows them.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: activation fixes the effect’s particulars and duration; dial: the user gives up ongoing control, and the effect ends at its specified limit.

rules.statement: Reflexive activation lets an eligible defense or sense switch on without a Ready or Concentrate maneuver. Activation is automatic unless the ability normally requires a roll, in which case the roll is at -4; successful activation while asleep wakes the user.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: activation responds automatically or uses a roll at -4; dial: the modifier is limited to defenses, concentration-based senses, and similar uses.

rules.statement: When a temporary mental disadvantage is made unavoidable, using the ability immediately produces the effects of a failed self-control roll. Price the disadvantage as 2.5 times its listed cost, dropping fractions; for example, a -10-point disadvantage gives a -25% limitation.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: every use causes the specified disadvantage effects; dial: the limitation’s value scales from 2.5 times the disadvantage’s cost.

rules.statement: An ability that needs concentration to control can be configured to run without attention after its initial activating maneuver. Its effects last for minutes equal to the success margin, or the ordinary duration if shorter, and continue even if the user is incapacitated or killed; the user cannot end or alter them early.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect runs independently for its defined duration; dial: the user loses all control after activation.

rules.statement: A ranged attack’s projection point and physical shape determine which aiming specialty applies: continuous streams use beam, breath, or gaze according to whether they emerge from hands, mouth, or eyes, while solid shots and separate bolts use projectile. The GM can assign or create a specialty for attacks that do not fit those forms; making a burning attack tightly focused changes no point cost.
locators: GURPS Powers: Special Effects: Beam, Breath, and Bolt (p. 113) (gurps-powers#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the specialty matching the attack’s delivery and shape; dial: GM may assign another; the distinction is cosmetic and does not change cost.

rules.statement: Cosmetic details cannot provide a useful capability by themselves. A player may, with GM approval, add one or two minor benefits related to the ability, but must accept an equal number of minor drawbacks; these can be represented as perks and quirks, with quirks imposing small penalties on the user or modest bonuses for opponents.
locators: GURPS Powers: Minor Benefits and Drawbacks (p. 115) (gurps-powers#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: forbid cosmetic effects that function as useful abilities; dial: allow matched minor perks and quirks; the trade-off is a small penalty or increased exposure.

rules.statement: A built-in restriction can be removed only by giving up a roughly equivalent normal benefit; the GM can require further omissions to balance the exchange or reject it. If the exchange is not comparable, it is not allowed as a special effect.
locators: GURPS Powers: Minor Benefits and Drawbacks: Omissions (p. 115) (gurps-powers#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain built-in restrictions; dial: exchange one for a comparable benefit; the lost benefit pays for the added freedom.

rules.statement: When assembling an ability, remove incompatible modifiers and limitations that duplicate built-in restrictions, and check that the remaining modifiers are mutually compatible. If the net limitation exceeds -80%, cap it at -80%; round fractional point costs up.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply only valid, non-duplicative modifiers and cap net limitation at -80%; dial: the GM can resolve conflicting enhancements with Selectivity; the cap prevents excessive discounting.

rules.statement: When two constructions produce the same capability, choose the one that best matches its explanation; if neither is a better fit, choose the simpler build, and if both are equally suitable and simple, choose the cheaper one. The GM may restrict or forbid a bargain-priced option if it is less useful than its apparent price suggests.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: favor accurate fit, then simplicity, then low cost; dial: GM may restrict or ban a loophole; the cheaper construction may lack important capabilities or protections.

rules.statement: An Energy Reserve is tied to a particular power source and can pay that source’s abilities’ basic fatigue costs, added fatigue costs, and extra-effort or stunt expenditures; it can also fuel related skills. It does not protect against ordinary fatigue, and only those associated powers can deplete it; it recharges one point per 10 minutes independently of rest.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reserve energy is source-specific and replenishes at one point per 10 minutes; dial: limit it to abilities, one power, stunts, or slower/no timed recharge; these restrictions limit what can draw on the reserve or how quickly it returns.

rules.statement: An air-based ability affects gases only, excluding dust, plasma, and supernatural or superscience ether. An attack that shapes existing air takes a -5% environmental limitation, and allowed innate attacks must inflict crushing damage with forms and modifiers appropriate to air jets, concussion waves, or tornadoes, subject to GM approval.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: confine the power to true gases and suitable crushing attacks; dial: GM chooses eligible attack forms; shaping existing air costs -5%.

rules.statement: Animal-control abilities that involve direct mental contact require a -25% restriction to animals only and work solely on ordinary, nonsapient animals. The power does not affect sapient or supernatural creatures.
locators: GURPS Powers: Sample Powers: Animal Control (p. 122) (gurps-powers#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: target only ordinary, nonsapient animals; dial: animal-only direct-contact abilities take a -25% restriction; the target class limits the effect.

rules.statement: Antipsi can interfere with any ability carrying the Psionic power modifier, regardless of its focus, and its own emissions may be immune to effects that block psi, including antipsi. Its talent may be absent, and in some settings the power is always random and uncontrollable.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: antipsi disrupts psionic abilities across focuses; dial: its talent may be unavailable and its effects may be random and uncontrollable; those limits make the interference unreliable.

rules.statement: Astral-only abilities with specified projection-related forms work only while the user is projecting; abilities with the relevant projection modifiers can likewise function during projection. The GM may also permit attacks that affect only insubstantial targets.
locators: GURPS Powers: Sample Powers: Astral Projection (p. 124) (gurps-powers#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: projection-restricted abilities work only during projection; dial: GM may allow insubstantial-only attacks; the projection state limits when the ability functions.

rules.statement: ESP information is resolved secretly by the GM: better rolls give better information, an ordinary failure yields no information, and failure by more than 5 produces false information.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial the severity of failed readings because false information can mislead characters.

rules.statement: Chaos and Order oppose one another: each can counter the other, and each includes defenses against the opposing power. Chaos effects can induce delirium, while Order can restore minds and bodies to inner peace.
locators: GURPS Powers: CHAOS, p. 125; ORDER, p. 133 (gurps-powers#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial how readily either power counters the other to match the setting’s balance of disorder and structure.

rules.statement: Force Constructs can create shaped force objects, barriers, attacks, or creatures, but projected creatures are not sentient. The constructs look somewhat unusual rather than like ordinary matter.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial what forms can be made because the projections are artificial force, not living beings.

rules.statement: Matter Control can reshape and finely alter inanimate objects, but cannot directly affect living beings. Its apparent ability to alter the user’s own body comes from effects that change matter touching the body.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial whether the power can affect living targets because the stated boundary excludes them.

rules.statement: Telepathy normally works only on living, sapient beings with IQ 6 or higher; attempts to affect machines or plants automatically fail. A GM may broaden its targets to all sentient minds with IQ 1 or higher if Animal Control is absent.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial the eligible minds because the usual target class is limited and settings may lack a separate animal-control power.

rules.statement: Machine Telepathy affects only machines with at least a rudimentary computer brain and never affects living beings. Its afflictions must be limited to electrical targets, with results interpreted as machine malfunctions such as standby, erratic operation, or shutdown.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial the range of machine effects because the power requires a computer-like mind and does not cross over to living targets.

rules.statement: Probability Alteration may suggest a particular fate for someone, but the GM decides what actually occurs, and the result appears as coincidence. Dictating the specific coincidence requires an additional Cosmic enhancement costing +300%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial from suggested outcomes to dictated coincidences, with precise control carrying the stated +300% cost.

rules.statement: Teleported attacks normally move a person or object in its entirety. Moving only part of a target or placing foreign matter inside the target requires a different attack construction, using an Affliction or an Impaling Attack with Malediction and, for the latter, Based on HT.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default; dial whether partial-target effects are permitted because they bypass the usual whole-target limit.

rules.statement: The GM may restrict Time Mastery characters to effects on only the past, only the future, or time’s flow in the present. The GM may also remove the ability to move physical objects through time by excluding sequential duplication and adding projection to time travel.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial; the GM limits temporal reach or object movement because unrestricted time powers can disrupt plots.

rules.statement: Vampirism can steal vitality, thoughts, dreams, abilities, or even bodily forms from living targets, but it cannot affect machines or other inanimate things. Its attacks need a suitable delivery limitation such as a curse-like effect, close contact, or a sensory condition.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restrict targets to living beings; dial: broaden the kinds of stolen traits or forms, paying the in-world cost of a suitable way to reach the victim.

rules.statement: Water users can create and manipulate water, including ice and steam, and may transform themselves into water; weather powers instead manipulate ambient humidity, pressure, and temperature to produce weather. Weather Control cannot produce unrelated elemental effects such as concussion waves, freeze rays, radio jamming, or transformation into flame.
locators: GURPS Powers: Water; Weather Control, pp. 135–136 (gurps-powers#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep each power within its stated material or atmospheric domain; dial: permit overlap with adjacent elemental effects, at the in-world cost of a less specialized source.

rules.statement: Weather-based attacks must use area coverage, overhead delivery, and bombardment; an attack that requires an already violent storm also has an environmental condition. A lightning call can bombard its area at skill 12, while the hailstorm example uses skill 10.
locators: GURPS Powers: Weather Control Abilities; Elemental Attacks, pp. 136–137, 139 (gurps-powers#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require broad, indirect delivery and an area; dial: remove the storm prerequisite or targeting limits, at the in-world cost of greater control.

rules.statement: Some attacks create persistent effects that last 10 seconds, while others end when a target leaves the affected area; the ice-slick effect requires a new resistance roll if the target returns. A sufficiently strong wind disperses the fog effect.
locators: GURPS Powers: Elemental Attacks; table notes, pp. 138–141 (gurps-powers#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make created areas temporary or vulnerable to their stated conditions; dial: extend duration or resistance to disruption, at the in-world cost of sustained power.

rules.statement: A successful energy-stealing touch transfers the victim’s lost fatigue points to the attacker on a one-for-one basis; life-stealing instead transfers lost hit points. Both are subject to the ordinary restrictions on the stealing ability.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: transfer only the amount drained and obey the ability’s ordinary restrictions; dial: increase the amount or speed, at the in-world cost of greater exposure or effort.

rules.statement: A distant psychic drain requires one minute of concentration per fatigue point transferred and a contest of will against will. While feeding, the attacker also takes on mental quirks or disadvantages chosen by the GM, totaling -10 points.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make the drain slow and impose the victim’s mental traits on the feeder; dial: speed feeding or reduce the borrowed burden, at the in-world cost of increased strain.

rules.statement: A curse can remain in force until the victim achieves a notable success, at which point it and the victim’s victory end together; ordinary curse-removal effects can also remove it. The example is resisted through a will-versus-will contest.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: tie the curse’s end to a meaningful success or a removal effect; dial: make it permanent, at the in-world cost of needing a stronger countermeasure.

rules.statement: A triggered death touch can leave a victim facing a heart attack at an unspecified future time and from any distance after failing a resistance roll. The victim escapes only by killing the attacker or persuading the attacker to cancel the effect; there is no ordinary cure.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: give the attacker control over whether the delayed effect is canceled; dial: allow independent cures, at the in-world cost of weakening the attacker’s hold.

rules.statement: A mental attack can erase all memories permanently, or selectively remove particular memories; hypnotism, shock treatment, or conditioning through mind control can reverse the effect. The attack is resolved as a contest of will against will.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make erasure permanent but reversible through specified interventions; dial: make selected memories harder to restore, at the in-world cost of a stronger attack.

rules.statement: For built-in attacks, the GM may require an Unusual Background costing 25, 50, or 100 points for capabilities comparable to increasingly destructive military weapons, and at least 200 points for strategic weapons. Alternatively, a weapon mount costs 2 points per mount, can hold one compatible weapon weighing no more than the user’s basic lift, and takes about five seconds to attach or remove; the weapon itself costs money and counts toward encumbrance.
locators: GURPS Powers: Arms Control; Weapon Mounts, p. 139 (gurps-powers#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: gate especially destructive built-in attacks by a steep access cost, while ordinary mounted weapons remain purchasable and removable; dial: relax the gate, at the in-world cost of greater campaign risk.

rules.statement: A gas effect fills a 2-yard radius on impact and drifts for 10 seconds. A target keeps making the initial resistance roll while exposed until failing or leaving; most gases call for a roll each second, while an onset effect is resisted on first exposure and again after each full onset interval.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: exposure is repeated while the target remains in the drifting cloud; dial: the interval and duration depend on the gas, at the cost of continued exposure.

rules.statement: Blistering gas can injure by skin contact or breathing: contact calls for HT-4 immediately and daily for a week, with each failure causing 1d injury; inhalation calls for HT-1 hourly for six hours, each failure causing 1d injury. The two injury tracks accumulate.
rules.speaker: rulebook
