rules.default_dial_reason: Default: separate exposure routes each impose recurring resistance and injury; dial: the route and cadence set how quickly the harm accumulates.

rules.statement: Nerve gas requires HT-5 resistance on contact immediately and once per minute for five minutes; each failure inflicts 2d injury. After total injury exceeds half the victim’s HP, the victim is paralyzed until healed.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated exposure checks can build to paralysis; dial: severe injury and a threshold make this a rapidly incapacitating, highly lethal effect.

rules.statement: Sleeping gas requires HT-2 resistance immediately and twice more at one-minute intervals; each failure costs 1d FP. The FP loss counts as missed sleep, and a victim reduced to 0 FP sleeps until recovering FP.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance failures drain fatigue in three checks; dial: fatigue loss becomes forced sleep at 0 FP, limiting further action.

rules.statement: A tranquilizer dart’s follow-up effect applies only if the dart inflicts at least some injury; the victim then rolls HT, and failure causes unconsciousness.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the secondary effect depends on the carrier penetrating and injuring the target; dial: armor can prevent both injury and the follow-up.

rules.statement: A defensive meta-trait can be recorded as one named defense with a fixed cost per level instead of listing its component abilities; additional levels stack. Power modifiers normally apply separately to each component, but the GM may apply them to the overall per-level cost to simplify accounting.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: levels add the bundled benefits; dial: applying modifiers to the whole package is a bookkeeping shortcut that may slightly change cost.

rules.statement: These body-surface defenses protect the user, not carried possessions. A projected force field generally extends far enough to cover the user’s equipment.
locators: GURPS Powers: Armor / Force Fields, pp. 145-146 (gurps-powers#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: bodily protection does not cover gear unless the defense is projected as a field; dial: equipment coverage follows the field’s extent.

rules.statement: A wall of force may be placed anywhere within 10 yards by taking an Attack maneuver; it forms a 6-yard-long, 1-yard-thick barrier in any shape, with DR 6 and 1 HP per level. It is rigid but does not injure collisions.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the barrier is a placed, finite obstacle with durability; dial: its dimensions and durability limit what it can block, and collision itself causes no harm.

rules.statement: A wall of matter works similarly to the force wall, but is made of solid material and collision with it can injure those who hit it.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a solid barrier can injure on collision; dial: this added consequence distinguishes it from a harmless rigid force barrier.

rules.statement: A door through a barrier up to 1 foot thick requires a second of concentration and an IQ roll, and costs 1 FP to open plus 1 FP per minute to keep open.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: opening and maintaining passage both consume fatigue; dial: thickness and duration constrain where and how long the route can remain available.

rules.statement: A gate between worlds requires users to be free to walk through it; the creator cannot simply vanish through the transition. A space portal links two points, but the destination must have been visited or be visible.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: travel requires physically traversing the gate and a known or visible destination; dial: those access conditions limit who can use it and where it can lead.

rules.statement: When a maintained ability that needs constant concentration is disrupted by an active defense or resistance roll, a self-control roll, falling, injury, or an affliction, its user must make a Will-3 roll; failure switches it off. Stun or stopping concentration ends it automatically.
locators: GURPS Powers: Distraction and Injury, p. 156 (gurps-powers#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: interruptions threaten concentration; dial: apply the Will-3 check only to abilities requiring it; cost: failure ends the active effect.

rules.statement: Unconsciousness immediately ends active switchable abilities unless their underlying traits explicitly remain active, while passive switchable abilities follow a setting chosen when acquired. Transient abilities cannot be triggered while unconscious, but an effect already produced by one generally runs its full duration; some lingering effects, such as those from Affliction, can persist after their source ends.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: unconsciousness ends active effects; dial: passive abilities may be set to switch off, stay on, or keep their state; cost: the character cannot act while unconscious.

rules.statement: Interference, a violated required disadvantage or pact, a missing required environment, or another failed limitation can shut an ability off immediately. Unless the underlying trait makes a permanent change or has a separate residual duration, its effects end too.
locators: GURPS Powers: Power Modifier Effects / Limitations, p. 157 (gurps-powers#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a failed condition suspends the ability and its effects; dial: specify the relevant condition and how quickly it takes effect; cost: violating it removes the benefit.

rules.statement: An ability may be temporarily crippled after a critical failure on an active use: roll HT for a physical ability or Will for a mental one. On failure it is unavailable for minutes equal to the margin of failure, followed by recovery checks once per minute; critical failure makes it unavailable for 1d months. Passive abilities are exempt except during active use, and crippling one ability also cripples its alternative-ability set.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: critical failures can cause temporary loss of access; dial: the GM may omit crippling or change its severity; cost: failure can disable an ability for minutes or months.

rules.statement: A controller using mental influence can order a subject to use abilities the subject consciously controls, but cannot command an impossible use or bypass an ability’s restrictions, interference, or crippling. The controller spends a Concentrate maneuver giving each set of orders; the subject acts on the next turn and regains control when the influence ends.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mental control can direct available abilities but cannot override their operating limits; dial: the influence determines what instructions can be imposed; cost: orders take time and the subject acts on a later turn.

rules.statement: When a controller possesses a body, the controller can use the host’s physical abilities and the controller’s own mental abilities, but not the host’s mental or the controller’s physical ones. When possession ends, each party regains its own abilities; continuing effects tied to a body stay with it, while effects tied to a mind follow that mind.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access depends on whether an ability belongs to the body or mind; dial: define where ongoing effects are anchored; cost: possession restricts which abilities each party can use.

rules.statement: With Multiple Feats, each active ability already on imposes -1 on rolls to actively use another ability from the same power. Transient abilities suffer this penalty but do not create it, passive uses neither suffer nor impose it, and penalties do not cross between powers.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: simultaneous active uses compete for control; dial: the GM may use or omit this optional rule; cost: each ongoing active ability makes further uses harder.

rules.statement: Under Repeated Attempts, after a failed activation roll the user may wait five minutes and try again without penalty. Trying sooner costs 1 FP and applies a cumulative -1 per attempt; after a success, further attempts at that feat cost no FP and add no penalties, but the current penalty remains until five minutes pass.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failed attempts strain and unsettle the user; dial: this optional rule applies to active-ability activation attempts; cost: quick retries consume FP and worsen the roll.

rules.statement: Extra effort can raise a quantifiable effect by a chosen percentage, up to 100%, with a Will roll at -1 per 5% increase or fraction; using a power adds Talent and emergencies give +5. It costs 1 FP for an instantaneous use or per minute for a maintainable one; a critical failure makes the task fail, briefly switches the ability off, and can cripple it.
locators: GURPS Powers: Extra Effort / Trading Fatigue for Effect, p. 160 (gurps-powers#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: pushing an ability increases its output at fatigue and failure risk; dial: the GM decides which abilities may use extra effort; cost: FP, a control roll, and possible shutdown or crippling.

rules.statement: Instead of increasing an ability’s effect, a user may spend 1 FP for a one-time +1 to an activation or Quick Contest roll, up to +4. This option does not apply to passive abilities or abilities used through an attack roll, and it carries no risk of catastrophic failure.
locators: GURPS Powers: Trading Fatigue for Skill, p. 161 (gurps-powers#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: extra effort can improve control rather than output; dial: allow up to +4 only for eligible active abilities; cost: 1 FP per bonus point.

rules.statement: For power abilities, an active-use roll is at -1 for each other active ability of that power already on. Transient effects that have ended do not count as still active, even if their consequences remain.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: maintaining several active effects divides attention; dial: penalties apply only within the same power and not to passive uses; cost: simultaneous active abilities reduce effective skill.

rules.statement: Active abilities can be detected through ordinary senses, while passive abilities generally require a special sense. Unless an ability is inherently invisible, wholly passive, or has No Signature, its user must define an ordinary-sense effect that witnesses notice automatically when unobstructed; special senses may also detect active uses by their source or focus.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: active use leaves a detectable trace; dial: No Signature or special senses alter detection; the in-world tradeoff is concealment versus visible evidence.

rules.statement: Normally passive defenses can be used actively once per turn as a power defense, if the relevant requirements are met. Such a use counts as active use of the ability for detection, costs, and use limits; a power defense is unavailable if the user made an All-Out Attack or does not know about the attack.
locators: GURPS Powers: Defending with Powers, p. 167 (gurps-powers#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: defenses protect passively; dial: active reinforcement or evasion is permitted subject to one power defense per turn; the cost is exposing the use to normal limits.

rules.statement: A power dodge is allowed when an instantaneous switchable movement ability or physical transformation can make an attack pass harmlessly by. Roll against Basic Speed + 3 + half Talent, rounding down; success avoids the attack, failure means it lands before activation, but either way the ability activates and counts as an active use.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no special dodge from an ability; dial: instantaneous movement or transformation can evade; the cost is an active use and its associated expenditure and limits.

rules.statement: An innate attack may parry another if the powers share a focus or are opposed, provided the parrying ability is accessible and can activate immediately. On success, subtract the defender’s damage from the attacker’s; any remainder hits the defender, while equal or greater defensive damage prevents harm.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: attacks do not cancel one another; dial: shared focus or opposed powers permit a parry; the cost is a defense attempt and possible residual damage.

rules.statement: A power block can reinforce an applicable damage resistance, resistance bonus, Control, or Obscure against qualifying attacks. Success doubles usual DR or resistance bonuses, or grants Control/Obscure one DR or resistance point per level; failure removes even the defense’s normal effect, and the attempt counts as active use.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: passive protection works at its ordinary strength; dial: a qualifying power can reinforce it; the gamble risks losing even the normal defense on failure.

rules.statement: For a contested resistance test, the defender may spend up to 4 FP after learning whether the attacker succeeded, gaining +1 to that resistance roll per FP spent. The points are spent even if the bonus does not change the result.
locators: GURPS Powers: Trading Fatigue for Resistance, p. 169 (gurps-powers#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance uses the usual roll; dial: up to 4 FP can improve a single contest; the in-world cost is immediate fatigue.

rules.statement: A group can combine powers only when everyone shares the same source; members link by physical contact or an appropriate mental link, then each concentrates and rolls IQ. The roll takes a penalty equal to the number of other participants, with bonuses for Talent and for a group sharing the same power; mental links impose an additional penalty if one-way.
locators: GURPS Powers: Combining Powers—Linking Up, pp. 170–172 (gurps-powers#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: abilities remain individual; dial: same-source participants can link and contribute; the cost is coordination, concentration, and a risk of failed or disrupted linkage.

rules.statement: While linked, the group chooses a leader for each task, who uses their own rolls and abilities with contributions from the others: matching abilities add half or a quarter of other levels, and Talent contributes by corresponding fractions. Any FP cost may be shared, but each use counts against every member’s use limits, and a critical failure affects everyone.
locators: GURPS Powers: Combined Powers in Action, pp. 172–173 (gurps-powers#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each user supplies only their own ability; dial: linked users pool capability and divide fatigue; the cost is shared use-limit consumption and collective critical-failure risk.

rules.statement: A user may temporarily add suitable enhancements to an ability after defining the intended effect and getting GM approval. It takes a Concentrate maneuver and Will roll for a mental ability, or Ready and HT for a physical one; the penalty is -1 per 10% added or part thereof, Talent helps, and each attempt costs 2 FP plus any voluntarily spent to offset penalties.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: abilities retain their purchased configuration; dial: a simple, source-consistent enhancement can be improvised; the cost is 2 FP, possible extra FP, and a roll penalty.

rules.statement: A successful temporary enhancement gives a transient ability one use, or an ongoing ability one minute; ongoing use can continue by making another roll and paying FP each minute. Failure leaves the ability functioning normally without the enhancement; critical failure disables it for 1d seconds and may cripple the whole power.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no temporary modification; dial: successful improvisation lasts one use or one minute, renewable with rolls and FP; the risk is temporary shutdown or power-wide crippling.

rules.statement: For a temporary attack enhancement, Area Effect may gain any number of levels if the attack already has it; Armor Divisor can be added to attacks except area effects, cones, and explosions. A Cone enhancement may be added to an attack without Cone, but its width is limited to one yard.
locators: GURPS Powers: Using Abilities at Default, p. 172 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit temporary changes within these limits; dial: exclude listed attack forms and cap a newly created cone at one yard, reflecting limited control.

rules.statement: Cyclic may provide two or three applications at intervals of no more than 10 seconds for Corrosion or Burning Attacks that do not normally endure. Persistent or Selective Area may be temporary additions to attacks with Area Effect; Drifting and Mobile may accompany Persistent.
locators: GURPS Powers: Using Abilities at Default, p. 172 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow the specified temporary area and repeated-hit options; dial: restrict cycles to two or three and intervals to 10 seconds or less.

rules.statement: A temporary enhancement must not change an attack’s basic effects in the world, and the GM may forbid options that would do so. Passive abilities generally cannot be temporarily enhanced, except when actively used; always-on defenses are generally excluded, with Affects Others plus Area Effect allowed for Force Fields and Mind Shields.
locators: GURPS Powers: Using Abilities at Default / Extending Defenses, pp. 172–173 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preserve an ability’s fundamental operation; dial: allow only stated active-use and defense exceptions, because passive protection is not normally under conscious control.

rules.statement: A character may improvise a related ability from an active ability only if the proposed effects are specified, the connection is plausible, and both abilities belong to the same power. The improvised ability must share the source modifier and every use limitation of the starting ability, and its final point cost cannot exceed the starting ability’s.
locators: GURPS Powers: Using Abilities at Default, pp. 172–173 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permit related improvisation; dial: require shared source, limitations, and no greater point value, representing the starting ability’s boundaries.

rules.statement: Attempting an improvised ability takes Concentrate and a Will roll if the starting ability is mental, or Ready and a HT roll if it is physical. The roll takes -2 per 25% of the starting ability’s cost represented by the new ability, or fraction, plus -2 if they are different general types; spending 1 FP cancels 1 point of penalty, and power Talent may be added.
locators: GURPS Powers: Using Abilities at Default, p. 173 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow the attempt; dial: charge a maneuver, a roll, and escalating penalties, with FP and Talent providing bounded assistance.

rules.statement: Every improvisation attempt costs 3 FP in addition to any voluntarily spent. Success gives one use if the effect is transient, or one minute if ongoing, after which another roll and FP payment are required; critical success waives the FP cost for that use or minute.
locators: GURPS Powers: Using Abilities at Default, pp. 173–174 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: successful improvisation works for a limited period; dial: require 3 FP and repeated rolls and costs for continued operation.

rules.statement: An improvised ability imposes -2 on all rolls it requires because the user is unfamiliar with it; lacking the relevant skill means using that skill at default, and the penalties stack. Failure produces no effect while leaving the starting ability normal; critical failure takes even an always-on ability offline for one second and requires a crippling check affecting the whole power.
locators: GURPS Powers: Using Abilities at Default, pp. 174–175 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: improvised use can succeed; dial: impose unfamiliarity and skill penalties, with critical failure risking a brief power outage and broader harm.

rules.statement: Against a biological power, an attacker who has observed it and succeeds at an appropriate obscure skill roll may target it at -8 with an impaling, piercing, or tight-beam burning attack. A major wound, calculated as torso injury, cripples the ability; recovery follows the crippling-duration rules and may be permanent.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a studied biological ability can be attacked; dial: require observation, a qualifying skill, a -8 attack, and a major wound.

rules.statement: For divine abilities, no sanctity makes them unusable; low sanctity gives activation rolls -5, while normal, high, or very high sanctity leaves them operating normally.
locators: GURPS Powers: Special Rules for Divine Powers, p. 175 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: abilities work in ordinary or favorable sanctity; dial: low sanctity imposes -5 and none prevents use, reflecting the deity’s domain.

rules.statement: For spirit abilities, a reaction of Neutral or better permits an attempt; a worse reaction forbids it and gives later invocations a cumulative -1 reaction penalty. Critical failure is treated as a Poor initial reaction, or Very Bad if extra effort was involved; extra effort costs HP instead of FP when blood is the required offering.
locators: GURPS Powers: Special Rules for Spirit Powers, p. 177 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spirits may permit an invocation; dial: reactions can bar use and worsen later chances, while blood-based effort spends HP.

rules.statement: Remote spirit effects require a representation of the absent target, with penalties of -1 for video or DNA, -2 for a photo or blood, -3 for hair or fingernails, -4 for clothing, -6 for a drawing, and -10 without a representation. Ritual delay can offset penalties: changing seconds to minutes, minutes to hours, or hours to days gives +3; two steps give +5 and three give +7.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: remote effects need a link to the subject; dial: weaker or absent representations impose increasing penalties, while longer rituals can compensate.

rules.statement: A psi’s powers remain with the mind when it moves to a body with a different brain, but the current brain must function properly. Optionally, major eye or skull wounds require a HT roll for each psi power, and suffocation, surgery, or drugs require one if they cause more than half HP of brain damage; failure has the usual crippling result.
locators: GURPS Powers: Special Rules for Psionic Powers, p. 177 (gurps-powers#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the mind retains its powers across bodies; dial: a damaged or nonfunctional brain can prevent use or cripple powers.

rules.statement: A power modifier can be defined so that detectors identify its users and devices suppress only powers carrying that modifier; it can also impose backlash and loss of control, making use unpleasant or dangerous.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a source-specific modifier; dial up detection, suppression, or dangerous instability when the setting treats that source as a liability.

rules.statement: Powers that share a source need not all be permitted: a setting may define what kinds of effects fit that source, and GMs may exclude abilities that do not. Low-powered campaigns may require concentration, time, short range, or unreliability, and may bar powers above a chosen level.
locators: GURPS Powers: p. 183, Power Games; p. 184, Possible Origins / What’s Allowed (gurps-powers#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to abilities consistent with the setting’s origin rules; dial down scope and reliability to keep inexperienced users’ powers constrained.

rules.statement: The GM may set an upper limit on attack damage and should check that characters can survive at least a couple of typical attacks; characters relying on evasion rather than toughness should still be able to survive one unlucky hit.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a damage ceiling and survivable encounters; dial toughness and attack limits to match the campaign’s danger level.

rules.statement: If a supernatural transformation changes a person’s nature in a way rejected by the power’s granting deity, the character loses those divine powers; innate abilities may also be erased if the transformation remakes the person’s spiritual essence, while other powers can survive.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to checking transformed nature against the power’s source; dial which power families are lost according to how deeply the change alters the person.

rules.statement: A linked pair succeeds automatically when using telepathic abilities on each other; the GM may extend this benefit to other fundamentally telepathic effects.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to automatic success only for the defined mental link; dial the covered effects if the bond is meant to support broader communication.

rules.statement: If a spell that normally resists another spell is used against a magical power that functions without a roll, the power-user resists with the better of IQ or Will, plus applicable Talent; the example totals 15 from IQ 12 and Talent 3.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a resistance roll based on the user’s stronger mental trait and relevant expertise; dial the outcome through the power’s applicable Talent.

rules.statement: Detection spells can reveal different layers of magical power: one can identify magic operating on or through an object, another can identify powers used within the last five seconds, and a third can reveal what powers are currently operating and give a useful indication of their function.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to distinguishing present operation from recent use; dial the detail of the reading while keeping the exact function only approximately identifiable.

rules.statement: A counterspell affects a power only when the caster possesses the same ability, as judged by the GM; a dispelling effect can negate a wider range of abilities. Other wards and countermeasures generally affect powers only when their limitations make them susceptible, or when a particular spell specifically opposes them.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to narrow, ability-matched countering and broader dispelling; dial other counters according to explicit susceptibility or a specific opposition rule.

rules.statement: A protective boundary can keep spirit powers from crossing it, resolved by a Quick Contest between the boundary’s skill and the user’s IQ plus Talent, or by the spirit’s attributes when those are known.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a contest at the boundary; dial access by the spirit’s or user’s capability, with the protection limited to crossing the marked space.

rules.statement: A faith-based aura may exclude evil divine or moral effects and effects relying on unlawfully summoned spirits within one yard; the protection has limits, and the source notes that rarity makes it unnecessary to increase the power modifier’s limitation.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-yard exclusion for the specified hostile effects; dial which principles count as opposed, since the protection is bounded and uncommon.

rules.statement: When powers are so dangerous or difficult to use that most people avoid them, treat their use as effectively rare; they may affect emergencies, while habitual use is largely limited to risk-takers and fanatics.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make dangerous powers uncommon in practice; dial: raise or lower the hazard; the in-world cost is injury, collateral harm, or fear of use.

rules.statement: If powered people can cancel one another’s effects, opposing sides may neutralize direct power use, leaving investigation or social manipulation as the practical ways to achieve their aims.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: let comparable powers counterbalance; dial: vary how often and how completely they cancel; the in-world cost is that raw power stops deciding the conflict.

rules.statement: In a secret-power setting, users must preserve secrecy or risk exposure, and greater visible power can make a character less effective because attention and countermeasures increase.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: secrecy constrains open use; dial: set how quickly exposure brings consequences; the in-world cost is lost privacy, exploitation, hostility, or countermeasures.

rules.statement: When a campaign shifts from having no powers to having them, the GM can give each PC a point allowance to choose a power or grant each one a specified power; the specified option gives the GM tighter control over what becomes available.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make new powers a deliberate campaign change; dial: choose player selection or a fixed grant; the in-world cost is disruption to the prior game’s expectations.

rules.statement: A god may lend a mortal some of its power through reenacting the god’s legend, sometimes involving a spirit journey; the process can also change the hero significantly.
locators: GURPS Powers: Mythic Fantasy Genre Conventions (p. 205) (gurps-powers#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: borrowed divine power requires a mythic undertaking; dial: decide how much power and lasting change it brings; the in-world cost is the journey and its personal consequences.

rules.statement: Gods can be constrained by family ties, vows, and rulings of higher gods, rather than acting without limits.
locators: GURPS Powers: Mythic Fantasy Genre Conventions (p. 205) (gurps-powers#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: divine action is bounded by obligations and authority; dial: set which ties or rulings bind a deity; the in-world cost is restricted freedom of action.

rules.statement: A god may avoid attacking mortal heroes directly because of sportsmanship or divine law, while still threatening them through agents and indirect control; a friendly patron may likewise be unable or unwilling to rescue them freely.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: divine power is constrained by rules of engagement; dial: decide how strict the limits and exceptions are; the in-world cost is that gods must use indirect means rather than settle matters themselves.

rules.statement: A place of power can provide a small zone of higher mana that a wizard can control and defend; possessing one may tie characters to that location.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a place of power offers a localized advantage; dial: define its size and mana benefit; the in-world cost is pressure to stay and defend it.

rules.statement: A setting may make particular spells unavailable when they violate an absolute rule of the world, such as the impossibility of escaping mortality or casually traveling to divine realms.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: disallow effects that contradict core world laws; dial: choose which laws are absolute; the in-world cost is that some desired outcomes cannot be achieved by spellcasting.

rules.statement: A GM who wants a normally prohibited or disruptive spell to remain possible can raise its energy cost, make it obscure, or require a 50-point unusual background for a beginning character to know it; learning it may require a major quest.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make exceptional magic costly or difficult to access; dial: increase energy, obscurity, or prerequisites; the in-world cost is substantial effort, expense, or an extraordinary qualification.

rules.statement: In horror-focused play, powers should be limited enough that they cannot routinely overcome every threat, or they should impose a cost, usually a severe one.
locators: GURPS Powers: Horror and Monster-Only Powers, p. 210 (gurps-powers#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to narrow or costly powers; dial strength upward only if the group wants less fear and danger.

rules.statement: In a secret-powers campaign, powers should be fairly limited and tightly constrained by the campaign concept; a reason must exist to keep those who know about them from speaking publicly.
locators: GURPS Powers: By the Book: Secret Powers, pp. 214-215 (gurps-powers#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to restricted capabilities and enforced secrecy; relax either only if exposure is meant to change the setting.

rules.statement: In some settings, religious faith or strong unbelief can disable some powers.
locators: GURPS Powers: Secret Powers Antagonists, p. 216 (gurps-powers#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to no belief-based shutdown; enable it only where conviction has a real supernatural or ideological cost.

rules.statement: Some hidden locations, including other-dimensional realms, allow powers to be used more safely or effectively than usual.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to ordinary power performance; grant a local advantage only where the location itself justifies it.

rules.statement: Psi abilities can be inborn or gained through a special training method; a character may have varying innate potential but still need training to unlock effective use.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one clear source of access; combine aptitude and training when the campaign needs a staged path to power.

rules.statement: If magical contact creates a lasting connection, a formerly attached or closely contacting piece of a target can serve as a link through which magic affects that target. Blood may be treated as a particularly strong link.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Law of Contagion, p. 14 (gurps-thaumatology#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contact links persist; dial: make the link weaker or temporary; the in-world basis is the history of contact.

rules.statement: If resemblance creates a magical link, a lookalike or symbolic counterpart can be used to affect the thing it represents; a symbol may also serve as a channel for a related power.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Law of Sympathy, p. 14 (gurps-thaumatology#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: meaningful resemblance establishes a link; dial: require closer likeness; the in-world basis is perceived similarity.

rules.statement: Under the Doctrine of Signatures, a plant’s resemblance to a body part, animal, or object indicates a related medicinal or magical use. A suitable Herb Lore or Pharmacy (Herbal) roll at -2 can identify such materials, potentially without prior familiarity with them.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: More Magical Laws, p. 15 (gurps-thaumatology#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resemblance provides clues to an ingredient’s use; dial: make identification harder or narrower; the cost is the chance of misreading the sign.

rules.statement: A setting may make consequential magic repay its caster later, with good or harmful acts returning at three times their intensity. For strong magic, especially effects that alter luck or fate, the rules could grant the caster an automatic short-term Destiny, with the form of repayment unpredictable.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: More Magical Laws, p. 15 (gurps-thaumatology#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: significant magic risks an unpredictable threefold return; dial: limit repayment to strong or fate-altering magic; the cost is delayed consequences.

rules.statement: A consciousness that reshapes subjective reality can produce, channel, or negate energy without a meaningful energy-source limit. Its practical output may still be constrained by the user’s strength of will or imagination.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: will can create or negate arbitrary energy; dial: constrain output by will or imagination; the in-world limit is the user’s capacity to conceive and impose change.

rules.statement: A campaign can cap Magery at a chosen level; three levels is offered as a common ceiling, while two is more restrictive and one or Magery 0 excludes progressively more spells. A cap restricts maximum casting power for spells whose energy depends on Magery, and makes high skill levels harder to reach.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: set a ceiling to constrain magical output; dial: choose the cap, with three levels a common option; the in-world limit is a mage’s maximum capacity.

rules.statement: Limited levels of Magery function only in their specified circumstances, so a mage may have less effective power at other times; if the restriction affects all Magery, the mage may temporarily be unable to cast spells or use Magery’s other benefits. A spell with a Magery-level prerequisite can generally be learned if the required level is available at some point during the year, though the GM may reject combinations whose qualifying moments are too rare.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Limited and Modified Magery, pp. 20-21 (gurps-thaumatology#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restrictions reduce available Magery outside their qualifying circumstances; dial: decide whether rare qualifying periods suffice for learning; the in-world cost is limited access to power.

rules.statement: With the Can’t Maintain Spells limitation, a caster can cast spells normally but cannot extend them beyond their initial duration by feeding in more energy, including through Maintain Spell or a similar method.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Special Limitations: Can’t Maintain Spells, p. 23 (gurps-thaumatology#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spells end at their initial duration; dial: omit the limitation for casters able to maintain effects; the cost is losing continuing benefits.

rules.statement: With the Can’t Use External Energy limitation, a caster must pay from personal reserves and cannot draw extra energy from items, substances, sacrifices, or energy-granting spells. The caster may still participate in ceremonial casting and use spells to recover personal energy after casting.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Special Limitations: Can’t Use External Energy, p. 23 (gurps-thaumatology#002)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: external energy cannot supplement the caster; dial: allow specified outside sources; the in-world cost is relying on the caster’s own reserves.

rules.statement: Magic granted by a god or spirit may be withdrawn if the recipient misuses it or loses the patron’s favor. The arrangement can require the recipient to act for the patron, with the possibility of sharing the patron’s enemies.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a patron’s gift depends on favor and service; dial: make the gift less vulnerable to loss of favor; the in-world cost is obedience and exposure to the patron’s conflicts.

rules.statement: With this restriction, every spell must be cast ceremonially; if all Magery has it, sensing a magic item requires a minor ceremony of at least 10 seconds before touching it. The stated limitation is -40%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ceremonial-only casting; dial: -40% and a 10-second minimum for item sensing; the time and ritual requirements make this poor for urgent or combat magic.

rules.statement: Cyclical Magery is unavailable during part of a repeating cycle, with its limitation value based roughly on the fraction of time it is unavailable, reduced somewhat because a mage may plan around it. Examples include -40% when available half the time, -5% for lunar absence lasting about 10% of the month, and -80% when available only two or three days per lunar month.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: power availability follows a cycle; dial: set the unavailable fraction and how often the cycle changes; infrequent or predictable downtime is easier to plan around.

rules.statement: This restriction leaves casting otherwise normal but weakens its ability to penetrate resistance: each level multiplies a target’s Magic Resistance by 1 plus the limitation level, or gives a target without Magic Resistance a resistance-roll bonus equal to that level. Magic items made by the mage retain the weakness for anyone using them; the cost is -5% per level, with four to six levels suggested as a maximum.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Easily Resisted Magery, p. 25 (gurps-thaumatology#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance is harder to overcome; dial: -5% per level; the drawback matters most when targets commonly resist magic.

rules.statement: A mage with this restriction may learn spells from any college but cannot cast them normally, only enchant them into items. The limitation is -30%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell knowledge can produce enchanted items but not direct spell effects; dial: -30%; this suits a stationary craftworker more than an adventurer who needs immediate magic.

rules.statement: A mage with this restriction cannot spend personal Fatigue Points on magic and must use outside sources, such as power-storing stones or allies lending power. The GM sets the limitation according to the availability and cost of those sources; -60% is usually appropriate, and this restriction cannot be combined with the opposite restriction on external energy.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: External Sources Only, p. 25 (gurps-thaumatology#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magical energy must come from outside the mage; dial: usually -60%, adjusted for source access and expense; the mage risks being unable to cast when supplies or helpers are absent.

rules.statement: Each level makes the required spellcasting ritual one category more complex, to a maximum of three levels, without changing casting time or energy cost. At least a spoken word and small gesture are always required, regardless of skill; the limitation is -10% per level and cannot be combined with Easy Casting.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ritual demands increase by one category per level; dial: up to three levels at -10% each; increasingly elaborate gestures and speech can be obstructed during a casting.

rules.statement: Spells with ongoing or supposedly permanent effects end as though reversed or dispelled after 1d hours, regardless of energy spent; instantaneous effects, including damage and restoration, are unaffected. Limited-use enchanted creations fade after 2d days, while unlimited-use items last 2d weeks; the limitation is -20%.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Fading Spell Effects, p. 25 (gurps-thaumatology#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lasting magic expires on a short schedule; dial: -20% with the stated 1d-hour, 2d-day, and 2d-week durations; temporary benefits and items cannot be relied on long-term.

rules.statement: This restriction makes some or all magical energy expenditure come from the caster’s health instead of fatigue. If the first energy point of each casting and the first point for maintaining a spell must come from health, the limitation is -30%; if all magical energy comes from health, it is -50%. The GM may rule that this injury cannot be restored by first aid or magical healing, requiring natural recovery.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell energy costs bodily health in the stated share; dial: -30% or -50%, with optional restrictions on healing; the caster pays through injury and may need time to recover.

rules.statement: On a spell failure, the mage may attempt an immediate second skill roll, without range penalties but with other applicable modifiers, to turn the result into a normal failure; this version is -10%. With no such second roll every failure is critical, for -30%; a further version makes the GM roll three critical-failure results and choose the worst, for -50%. Casting and stabilization skill cannot exceed 15, and the mage pays full energy even for effects in low mana; this restriction cannot combine with Stable Casting.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Radically Unstable Magery, p. 27 (gurps-thaumatology#003)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: failures risk escalating consequences; dial: -10%, -30%, or -50%; the risk and full energy expenditure make unreliable magic costly even when its effects are weakened.

rules.statement: When Magery has this restriction, a higher power or other governing source may withdraw it if the mage violates its rules; unlike directly granted spell access, the mage still learns spells through ordinary prerequisites. The passage gives no fixed limitation value.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: power remains subject to an enforcer’s conditions; dial: the passage sets no value; the in-world cost is the risk of losing Magery for failing the governing code.

rules.statement: Once activated, restricted Magery remains functional for one minute; maintaining spells requires it to remain active unless local mana is high or better. A spell with time remaining does not end merely because the Magery becomes inactive.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: active Magery lasts one minute; dial: this duration and the local-mana exception; short active periods can interrupt maintenance but do not erase a spell that still has duration remaining.

rules.statement: A GM may require a Fright Check when a wizard learns a spell or gains Thaumatology skill; this can be limited to particular colleges. For advanced spells, apply a penalty equal to half the spell’s prerequisite count, rounded down, and especially fearsome spells may also trigger a check when cast.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: learning and casting need no fear check; dial: add checks, especially for advanced spells; the danger is harm to the wizard’s sanity or soul.

rules.statement: A GM may prohibit a spell from being learned above the skill level of its prerequisites, or replace the prerequisite structure with a shorter college-entry list, individual requirements, or different requirements reflecting the setting. When changing prerequisites, keeping roughly the same prerequisite count helps preserve the spell’s difficulty and availability.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Changing Prerequisites; The Prerequisite Count, pp. 33-34 (gurps-thaumatology#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spells require their listed prerequisites; dial: simplify, replace, or tighten those requirements; the tradeoff is access to powerful magic versus breadth of study and setting coherence.

rules.statement: Casting time may be multiplied—ceremonial casting multiplies it by 10, while other options include doubling or tripling it—or reduced for particular spells. A spell’s energy cost may also be raised or lowered; costs above 5, and especially 10 or more, generally require ceremonial casting unless an external energy source is available.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Casting Time and Energy Cost, pp. 34-35 (gurps-thaumatology#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use each spell’s listed time and cost; dial: change either or both; slower casting or scarce energy limits tactical use, while external energy can remove that constraint.

rules.statement: A GM may limit what a spell can do or require a special payment: examples include restoring only half the injury from each wound, requiring $200 of potions per HP restored, or consuming one unit of congealed magic per casting. A spell that makes the caster share a wound’s pain can also require a Will roll to cast and/or a Fright Check afterward.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Changing Effects; Special Costs, pp. 34-36 (gurps-thaumatology#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the spell’s standard effect and ordinary costs; dial: impose narrower effects or extra material and personal costs; difficult or costly magic is less usable, especially in the field.

rules.statement: For a spell with a permanent effect, the GM may require the caster to specify a mortal-achievable condition that can negate it; the condition must be discoverable or made possible by the universe. As an alternative for a limited-duration spell, a simple, identifiable negating condition may reduce its energy cost by 25%.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spells end or are removed by the usual means; dial: make a specified condition necessary to end an enduring effect, or trade easy negation for lower cost; this makes lasting magic vulnerable to a discoverable solution.

rules.statement: With flexible ritual rules, a caster can omit foot motions for -2 skill, use one hand for -2 or no gestures for -4, and speak softly for -2 or omit the incantation for -4. Especially precise motions and a loud, clear incantation take twice as long but give +1 skill; ritual omissions do not change energy cost or casting-time reductions.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: casting requires the usual words and gestures; dial: allow omissions at skill penalties or careful performance for extra time and a bonus; the caster trades reliability or speed for less conspicuous or less demanding rituals.

rules.statement: A spell unknown to the wizard may default to any known spell in the same college at -4, with a further penalty equal to the unknown spell’s prerequisite count. Add the known spell’s prerequisite count as a bonus if it lies in the unknown spell’s prerequisite chain; spells requiring an advantage the caster lacks cannot be cast this way, and default casting doubles normal energy cost and casting time.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a wizard casts only spells known to them; dial: permit penalized defaults within a college; broader improvisation costs twice the normal energy and time and may be unreliable.

rules.statement: A caster may add GM-approved enhancements to a spell by spending 1 extra energy and taking -1 effective skill per 5% of enhancements. The extra energy is part of the spell’s cost and is reduced normally by high skill; changes to duration, fatigue cost, or casting time, and Side Effect and Symptoms, are excluded, while Cosmic is allowed only for defense against cosmic attacks.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Trading Energy for Enhancements, p. 40 (gurps-thaumatology#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell effects use their listed form; dial: buy approved enhancements during casting; the caster pays with both energy and reduced casting skill, and some alterations are prohibited.

rules.statement: A wizard may reduce casting time by one second per 4 extra energy spent, but cannot reduce it below one second and cannot use this option for ceremonial magic. Alternatively, exchanging energy for effective skill gives +1 for 20% extra energy, +2 for 40%, +3 for 60%, +4 for 100%, then another +1 per further 100%; these skill increases do not reduce casting time, energy cost, or ritual requirements.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Trading Energy for Speed and Skill, p. 39 (gurps-thaumatology#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: casting uses listed time and skill; dial: spend more energy for speed or skill; this favors casters with substantial personal or external energy reserves.

rules.statement: A campaign may require spells to be available in a wizard’s grimoire. One suggested price is 2% of average starting wealth per spell, with all its prerequisite spells in the same book; without that requirement, the suggested price is 2% plus 1% times the spell’s prerequisite count. Copying a spell may take 1d-2 days, minimum one day, and a successful Thaumatology roll; with personal shorthand, learning may instead require weekly rolls whose success margins total the spell’s prerequisite count.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Grimoires; Gaining New Spells, p. 38 (gurps-thaumatology#004)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spell knowledge need not depend on a physical book; dial: restrict access to spells recorded in grimoires and charge wealth, time, and study; magic is limited by what a wizard can obtain and learn.

rules.statement: A wizard may cast an eligible spell using a known enhancement combination as an Average technique, whose maximum skill equals the underlying spell skill; improving the technique does not reduce its extra energy cost. The GM may require one perk per spell varied, per available enhancement, or per particular spell-and-enhancement combination.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: enhancement options are unavailable unless the campaign allows them; dial: require purchased access and skill investment; customization costs both character resources and the extra energy specified for the enhancement.

rules.statement: With the suggested cap, a wizard’s spell skill cannot exceed 10 + Magery; an alternative cap is 10 + twice Magery. The cap may be removed for enchantment alone, allowing a Magery 2 wizard to enchant using spells at skill 15 or higher while using effective skill 12 for other workings.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Minor Spell Variants, p. 41; Capped Spells and Enchantment (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cap spell skill by Magery; dial: raise the cap or waive it for enchantment, because broader limits make powerful wizards more costly.

rules.statement: Mixed tree spells require access to every college assigned to the spell and count as belonging to all of those colleges for prerequisite purposes. Learning them systematically also requires at least six spells from each relevant consonant college and three from each applicable vowel college.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Ogham Alphabet, p. 42; Mixed Tree Spells, p. 45 (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require access to every assigned college; dial: omit the extra study requirements, at the cost of less demanding specialist training.

rules.statement: The ethical-category sensing spell detects category rather than hostility, can detect objects as well as thinking beings, and on a critical success reveals the likely source of the category. It costs 1 energy per area unit, with a minimum cost of 2.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Ethics and Spells, p. 49; Sense (Ethical Category) (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: detect ethical category rather than intent; dial: decide which beings and objects can carry a detectable category, because alignment may be faint or absent.

rules.statement: Protection against an ethical category lasts 1 minute and can be cast only on a willing subject. Each energy point spent, up to 5, grants +1 DR and +2 Magic Resistance; maintaining it costs half the casting cost.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Ethics and Spells, p. 49; Protection from (Ethical Category) (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: protect only against attacks from the specified category; dial: decide whether indirect attacks qualify, because the instigator may not be the immediate attacker.

rules.statement: An ethical-category exclusion boundary lasts until broken and bars creatures of that category. It costs 1/2 energy per square foot protected, at least 5, and creatures forcing entry use (ST+IQ)/4 rather than (ST+IQ)/2.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Ethics and Spells, p. 50; Exclude (Ethical Category) (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: bar only the specified category; dial: include ordinary people strongly committed to it, because commitment may be supernatural or merely chosen.

rules.statement: The ethical-category loyalty spell lasts 1 hour and costs 2 energy to cast and 1 to maintain. Casting cost is not increased for an unknown subject, but is quadrupled if the subject is the caster’s foe.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Ethics and Spells, p. 50; Loyalty of (Ethical Category) (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply loyalty only to beings of the specified category; dial: use the foe surcharge as written, because coercing an enemy takes more power.

rules.statement: A magic-only Energy Reserve can power spells and other explicitly magical powers, but not ordinary activities; it may be combined with ordinary Fatigue Points in one spell. Spent reserve recovers at 1 point every 10 minutes regardless of rest, and can also be replenished by suitable energy-transfer effects.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Energy Sources, p. 50; “Magic Only” Fatigue (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep magical and ordinary fatigue separate; dial: allow other magical powers to draw on the reserve, because that broadens its uses.

rules.statement: Paut restores 1 point of magical-purpose fatigue per ounce, but does not restore fatigue lost to nonmagical activity. A drinker may consume 1 ounce per second, up to 6 times ST ounces in 24 hours; excess energy after reaching full fatigue remains available for magical use for 5 minutes.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Alternative Power Stores, p. 51; Paut (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treat the drink as a limited consumable source; dial: alter the daily dose limit, because production and ingredients constrain supply.

rules.statement: A Cone of Power can only be raised ceremonially; each participant contributes 1, 2, or 4 energy per hour in low, normal, or high mana. It takes 1 hour to begin, costs 6 energy to cast and 6 to maintain, and accumulates energy while the ceremony continues; after the first hour, participants can draw on it to start other spells on the next turn, but not to power the Cone itself.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Alternative Power Stores, p. 52; Raise Cone of Power (gurps-thaumatology#005)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: tie generation to ceremony duration and local mana; dial: let exertion double or triple contributions, because sustained ritual effort can increase output.

rules.statement: A fixed magical site supplies a defined amount of energy per interval, possibly rolled randomly, and may also impose a total-use cap over a longer period. Drawing on it can require a roll; critical results may increase the yield while risking temporary or permanent burnout, or make the site unusable for a time.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Static Power Supplies, p. 54 (gurps-thaumatology#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the site has a stated supply and draw procedure; dial: set its rate, cap, and burnout risk; in-world, drawing too much can exhaust or damage the source.

rules.statement: When several users draw from a fixed source at once, its flow may be divided equally, or they may contest control; the winner can hold control for an extended time, or users can contest again each turn. Residents or people who have studied the site may receive a bonus in the contest.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Static Power Supplies, p. 54 (gurps-thaumatology#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: concurrent access is shared or contested; dial: choose how long a victor retains control; in-world, familiarity with the place can confer an advantage.

rules.statement: A practitioner who is Very Blessed and follows at least a -10-point religious discipline can accumulate supernatural-use credit: prayer or sanctified meditation earns 1 point per 8 hours, study earns it at half that rate, and a virtuous life at a quarter rate. Notable meritorious acts may grant 25 points or less, and the credit can be saved, but cannot be combined with fatigue points or powerstones; an optional reserve ceiling is twice Will plus Power Investiture.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Meditation, Holiness, or Study, p. 54 (gurps-thaumatology#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: credit accrues from specified devotional practices and is kept separately; dial: allow an optional reserve cap and discretionary act awards; in-world, the credit represents favor or standing rather than ordinary energy.

rules.statement: Devotional credit may be restricted to item enchantment, which is usually completed within a day. The enchanter must succeed at every required symbol skill roll: failure preserves the credit but bars another attempt at that enchantment until the related skills improve, while critical failure may bar it permanently; 25 credit points can instead be converted to 1 character point for item creation.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the credit creates an item rather than powering general adventuring effects; dial: use symbol-based procedures and allow conversion to character points; in-world, inadequate knowledge can frustrate or permanently close the attempt.

rules.statement: A sacrifice can release energy for magic, but it destroys what is sacrificed; a created thing should not yield more energy than was spent making it, and repairing or resurrecting the sacrifice should invalidate the result or be impossible. Energy may be usable only briefly: requiring the caster to begin within 10 seconds and to have performed the sacrifice sharply limits how many sacrifices can fuel one casting.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Sacrifices: The Process; Energy Availability, pp. 54–55 (gurps-thaumatology#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: destruction yields energy that must be spent promptly; dial: permit holding it longer or pooling assistants’ contributions; in-world, the sacrifice’s vital essence is consumed or sent away.

rules.statement: One simple valuation for an inanimate sacrifice grants 1 energy point per 250 of its worth, measured against either average starting wealth or the caster’s starting cash for their Wealth level. A living sacrifice can instead be valued by a fixed amount, size or HP, intelligence, character points, or other specified traits; for example, 2 times HP gives a modest yield and 10 times HP a much larger one.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Inanimate Sacrifices; Living Sacrifices: Value, pp. 55, 58 (gurps-thaumatology#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: value is calculated from worth or a chosen creature trait; dial: select the valuation method and yield; in-world, the setting’s metaphysics determines what makes a sacrifice potent.

rules.statement: A living sacrifice can be nonlethal, but the payment may require HP loss, pain, or permanent injury; a permanent injury exchanged for a major benefit generally cannot be healed without also giving up that benefit. Sacrificial magic may also bring social or supernatural penalties, or distort later effects and the caster’s state.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Nonlethal Living Sacrifices; Living Sacrifices: The Price; Flavored Sacrificial Energy, pp. 57–58 (gurps-thaumatology#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: bodily harm or stigma can balance the benefit; dial: choose the severity, permanence, and supernatural taint; in-world, power is bought through suffering or a morally costly act.

rules.statement: A caster may use fixed spell slots instead of casting costs: at day’s start, the caster prepares a selection from a repertoire and forgets each spell as it is cast. One implementation uses limited-use spell-only modular abilities, often with preparation required; another uses focused Wild Talent, rolling against IQ plus Magery or the relevant power’s Talent to cast a chosen spell.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: daily prepared slots limit how many spells can be cast; dial: choose fixed preparation or a more flexible talent-based method; in-world, magical capacity is constrained by what the caster has prepared or can improvise.

rules.statement: In very low mana, only mages can cast, all spells take -10 to skill, and each attempt costs 1 extra personal FP before rolling; that extra cost cannot come from external stores. Magic items need Power 25 or more and cost the user 1 extra FP to activate; mana-dependent creatures suffer as if in no mana, but can roll HT to avoid HP loss and take only half damage if that roll fails.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Mana Levels: Very Low Mana, p. 58 (gurps-thaumatology#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the region weakens casting and adds personal costs; dial: use this extreme level as a local or world-wide condition; in-world, scarce ambient mana makes magic exhausting and suppresses dependent beings.

rules.statement: In wild mana, anyone without Magic Resistance can cast known spells even without Magery; any successful roll is a critical success costing 0 FP, while any failure is a critical failure and costs the spell’s normal energy. In twisted mana, spells take an additional -2, every failure is a critical failure, and even success costs 1 extra energy and twists the effect to inconvenience the caster.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Wild Mana, p. 59; Twisted Mana, p. 61 (gurps-thaumatology#006)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: wild mana makes success unusually powerful but failure catastrophic, while twisted mana makes casting costly and perverse; dial: choose the region’s size, rarity, and severity; in-world, unstable or hostile ambient magic makes casting dangerous.

rules.statement: When a person’s magic-warping trait affects only their own spells and magic cast on them, it cannot be switched off. Magic cast on them is distorted; even healing can be painful or inconvenient, and hostile magic can cause additional harm to the target without penalizing the caster. The trait is worth -15 points, or 0 in a campaign where magic is extremely rare.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Minor Spell Variants, pp. 61–62 (gurps-thaumatology#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is involuntary and makes magic on the person go awry; dial: it may be worth 0 when magic is extremely rare.

rules.statement: In its area-producing form, the trait creates a twisted-mana zone with a base radius of 2 yards. It affects allies and the bearer as well as enemy wizards; each level of Increased Area doubles the radius, and Switchable lets the bearer turn it on or off with a Ready maneuver.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Minor Spell Variants, p. 63 (gurps-thaumatology#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the zone reaches 2 yards and can disrupt magic for everyone nearby; dial: area can double per enhancement level, or the bearer can pay for the ability to switch it with a Ready maneuver.

rules.statement: Magic Resistance can coexist with Magery if it is improved, or if it is Switchable. With Switchable, the user can turn it on or off with a Ready maneuver, but can benefit from Magery and cast spells only while resistance is off; helpful spells also work fully on them in that state.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Magic Resistance and the Mage, p. 63 (gurps-thaumatology#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: active resistance blocks the user’s own spellcasting and benefits from helpful magic; dial: paying +100% for Switchable allows control, but changing state takes a Ready maneuver.

rules.statement: Magic Resistance does not protect against magical attacks that produce essentially ordinary physical injury, such as missile spells or magic weapons. A defense with Damage Resistance and Limited, Magic (-20%) can stop the magical portion of such damage; against a weapon whose magic adds 2 damage, it can remove those 2 points but not the weapon’s ordinary damage.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Resistance vs. Magically Based Damage, p. 63 (gurps-thaumatology#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance stops magic itself, not ordinary injury merely delivered by a magical source; dial: the specialized defense blocks only the magical component.

rules.statement: Clerical spells may be learned without prerequisites by spending points, including directly after prayer; a GM may instead require 200 hours of devout contemplation per new spell. A deity restricts the available spells by its portfolio and may alter or suspend a cleric’s powers, including making exceptions for particular circumstances.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the deity grants only a portfolio-limited spell set and can change or withdraw it; dial: spell acquisition may require 200 hours of contemplation.

rules.statement: Power Investiture replaces Magery for clerical spellcasting: it improves clerical spell skill and sets the per-turn energy limit for spells that have one, while Magery has no effect on those functions. Spells that normally require a Magery level usually require the same Power Investiture level when granted by a deity.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: divine spellcasting uses the cleric’s Investiture rather than Magery; dial: the GM may relax the matching-level requirement in selected cases.

rules.statement: During clerical ceremonial casting, a qualifying participant who has the relevant divine connection and knows the clerically granted spell at skill 15 or higher may contribute any amount of FP. Other qualifying assistants may contribute up to 3 FP each; willing spectators who occasionally worship the caster’s deity contribute 1 FP each, capped at 100 FP total, while opposing spectators subtract 5 FP each, capped at -100 FP total.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: participants’ devotion and spell qualification determine whether, and how much, energy they contribute; dial: spectator participation can be made stricter by the GM.

rules.statement: Sanctity functions like mana for clerical spells, with levels from none to very high; its level is specific to a deity and can differ by god in the same place. Clerics can sense a boundary or change in sanctity with an IQ + Power Investiture roll, at -3 if they were not watching or searching for it.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Sanctity; Sanctity Levels, pp. 69–70 (gurps-thaumatology#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: location-specific sanctity affects clerical spellcasting and may be sensed; dial: the GM decides how territorial gods and their alliances make sanctity vary.

rules.statement: An invested priest can temporarily raise a suitable space, typically about the size of a private room, to high sanctity for one full day by spending about an hour in prayer and purification with Religious Ritual. The space must be identified and must not already be sanctified to another deity or below normal sanctity for the priest’s god.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a short ritual creates high sanctity for one day in a bounded, eligible space; the location’s prior sanctity and dedication limit where it works.

rules.statement: Permanent sanctification requires a site controlled by the faith and normally a specially prepared or adapted location. A day or so of ritual by someone of Religious Rank 3 or higher is required; afterward, the site generally needs a priest to maintain it and a congregation to use it regularly.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: lasting high sanctity takes control of the site, preparation, and substantial ritual; continued religious use and care help sustain it.

rules.statement: A cleric’s critical failure in very high sanctity may temporarily lower the area’s sanctity by one level for 2d seconds, or until priests reconsecrate it and the caster makes atonement. It may instead prompt divine judgment on recent clerical lapses in the area.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Critical Failures on Clerical Magic, p. 70 (gurps-thaumatology#007)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a serious casting error can damage sacred space or draw divine scrutiny; dial: the GM chooses whether the loss lasts 2d seconds or until repair and atonement.

rules.statement: A cult member without Power Investiture cannot cast clerical spells where sanctity is below high; temple guardians are restricted to temples and shrines. Some spells additionally require a minimum Power Investiture level.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: access depends on sanctity and sometimes rank; dial: raise or lower the required sanctity or investment; in-world, divine power is available only in favored places or to sufficiently invested priests.

rules.statement: An ordinary or high priest, but no other person, can temporarily sanctify a blacksmith’s forge or metalworker’s workshop, or a small stone- or brick-walled room with a central fire. Open-air places cannot be sanctified, and temples or shrines have high sanctity while most of the world has normal sanctity.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: temporary sanctification is limited by who performs it and by enclosed, suitable spaces; dial: change eligible sanctifiers or locations; the restriction reflects the god’s association with hearths and craft.

rules.statement: A ritual magician learns a Very Hard core skill, then Very Hard college skills that default to it at -6 and cannot exceed it. Individual spells are Hard techniques defaulting from the college skill at a penalty equal to the spell’s prerequisite count, and cannot exceed that skill.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each layer limits the next, with a -6 college default and spell penalties tied to prerequisites; dial: alter the default or cap; in-world, ritual mastery requires both general grounding and specialized knowledge.

rules.statement: A ritual magician may attempt spells at default from any college studied, or even spells never studied, although penalties can accumulate from core skill through college skill to spell. Magery adds to the core, college, and spell levels only once when determining a spell’s level.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: broad access is offset by stacked penalties, and Magery is not counted repeatedly; dial: restrict spell access or change the bonus; in-world, general magical aptitude helps but does not multiply through the chain.

rules.statement: For spells that manipulate other spells, ritual magicians count as knowing a spell at the level at which they can cast it, including at default; if a point in the spell is required, casting it at skill 10 or higher suffices.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: [Page 73] Knowing Spells to Manipulate Them (gurps-thaumatology#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: manipulation uses actual casting competence, with skill 10+ standing in for a required point; dial: set a higher or lower competence threshold; in-world, affecting another spell demands practical familiarity with it.

rules.statement: One way to handle non-spell prerequisites is to require the ritual caster to possess them, treating Magery as Ritual Magery. Alternatively, each 10 full character points of required traits adds 1 to the spell’s prerequisite count; for example, this makes Lend Energy’s count 1 and Simple Illusion’s count 2.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the GM chooses between mandatory prerequisites and a point-cost-based penalty; dial: choose the stricter or more permissive method; in-world, prerequisites represent either necessary capabilities or added complexity.

rules.statement: A GM may change a spell’s prerequisite count to make it easier or harder at default; for example, reducing Enchant from 10 to 5 makes ritual item-making more attainable, while increasing Analyze Magic from 3 to 10 makes identification specialist work.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: [Page 74] Changing the Default Modifiers (gurps-thaumatology#008)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: listed prerequisite counts set difficulty; dial: adjust individual counts; in-world, magical traditions vary in how accessible particular practices are.

rules.statement: In ceremonial ritual casting, an assistant counts as a mage only if he has Ritual Magery and uses the same specialty of the same core skill as the leader. An assistant able to cast the spell at 15+ can contribute as much energy as he can spare; at skill 8-14, he contributes energy according to the ceremonial rules, while others contribute only 1 energy each.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shared casting rewards matching magical training and limits contribution by spell competence; dial: relax specialty matching or alter contribution thresholds; in-world, coordinated ritual requires a common method.

rules.statement: In threshold-limited magic, casting and maintaining spells add their adjusted energy cost to a running tally rather than spending FP. The suggested tally recovery is 8 points per day at sunrise, and a wizard’s suggested safe threshold is 30.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magic accumulates strain in a tally that recovers 8 daily against a threshold of 30; dial: change threshold, recovery, or recovery timing; in-world, drawing ambient power distorts the wizard’s relation to reality.

rules.statement: Whenever tally rises above threshold, the wizard makes a Calamity Check that turn; while above threshold, each turn of casting or adding tally for maintenance also requires a check. Roll 3d, adding 1 for each full 5 points above threshold after the casting; on a result of 29+, the spell fails unless the caster succeeds at Will with a penalty equal to that bonus.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: excess accumulated power triggers increasingly dangerous checks, with a possible spell failure at 29+; dial: change the threshold or escalation rate; in-world, overdrawn magic produces unpredictable backlash.
