rules.statement: A buffer object diverts tally increases that would otherwise affect its user, raising that user’s effective threshold by the number of points it can absorb. A created buffer has twice the capacity that the corresponding energy-capacity value would give a Powerstone, and it restores 1 point per fortnight in low mana or per 2 days in normal mana, with other rates following the same pattern.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: the GM may permit buffers; their finite capacity and slow recharge limit how much casting strain they can absorb.

rules.statement: Base threshold and recovery-rate values may differ among wizards, but their product must remain equal; the example combinations all produce 240. The GM may rule out extreme combinations that let a wizard cast a devastating spell and then wait weeks to recover.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: equal products preserve a shared baseline; extreme thresholds can enable disruptive bursts followed by long downtime.

rules.statement: In ceremonial casting, each participant’s tally is assessed by the usual accounting for energy contributed. An opposing spectator reduces the effective contribution by 5 and gains 5 tally personally, because engaging in the working exposes participants to cumulative calamity risk.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: opposition can hinder the working but transfers danger to the opponent through added tally.

rules.statement: Under emergency threshold casting, the campaign threshold is fixed at zero and cannot be improved, so every casting automatically requires a Calamity Check; recovery is generally kept to 1–10 points daily. The GM may restrict who can use this option, and access may require a 10-point Unusual Background.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Emergency Use of Threshold Casting, p. 81 (gurps-thaumatology#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: zero threshold makes every use dangerous; low recovery and possible access requirements constrain this emergency power.

rules.statement: A wizard may spend 4 FP for each point of spell energy that does not add to tally, allowing extra power without increasing calamity risk from tally. Alternatively, with the ‘Some Fatigue Cost’ option, every successful spell and every critical failure costs 1 FP in addition to the tally increase.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Trading Fatigue Points for Power; Some Fatigue Cost, p. 81 (gurps-thaumatology#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: fatigue can buy safer extra energy or limit repeated casting, at the cost of the caster’s physical reserves.

rules.statement: A wizard’s familiar can maintain its own tally, threshold, and recovery rate as a buffer for the wizard’s tally. A calamity may fall on the familiar, pass through to the wizard, or be assigned by a fixed rule or choice; loss of spellcasting ability should usually affect the wizard.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Familiars as Buffers, p. 82 (gurps-thaumatology#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: a familiar can absorb consequences, but has its own finite tolerance and may transmit harm through the bond.

rules.statement: For decanic casting, each pair of relevant zodiacal correspondences gives +1 effective skill and each pair opposing the spell gives -1; each three relevant planetary correspondences give +1 and each three opposing ones give -1. The combined zodiacal and planetary modifier is capped at +3, and the caster must deliberately involve the relevant place or material.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: symbolic correspondences can improve or hinder casting, but require deliberate use and are bounded by a +3 cap.

rules.statement: When casting across dimensional boundaries, apply -10 per boundary in addition to -5 for being unable to touch or see the target; at intersecting places the boundary penalty is only -5. These boundary penalties do not apply to Gate spells or summonings.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: distance between realms obstructs casting, while boundary-crossing spells are exempt because that is their purpose.

rules.statement: A caster can claim only the strongest applicable bonus under each of sympathy, names, and contagion, and their combined bonus cannot exceed +6. If a sympathetic link substitutes for ordinary range penalties, the caster still takes -5 for being unable to touch or see the target, and this does not let Missile spells be launched remotely.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: symbolic links can overcome distance, but capped bonuses and targeting limits prevent unrestricted remote attacks.

rules.statement: An unfamiliar language may require an IQ or Hidden Lore roll before spellcasting, at -1 for Accented or -3 for Broken comprehension. Common languages can impose up to -5, sacred languages give no modifier, and ancient languages may grant +3 while esoteric tongues grant at least +5; poetic casting can grant a skill bonus up to a recommended +6 but adds at least 2d minutes and can fail or penalize on a failed Poetry roll.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Magical Languages; Poetry, pp. 87–89 (gurps-thaumatology#009)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Dial: language and poetic form modify spell reliability; stronger forms demand fluency, preparation, time, or risk.

rules.statement: Unused materials can improve a spell’s correspondence bonus by +1 for each +3 in bonuses the material already provides. A caster who made, grew, or raised the material personally may add another +1; a stricter option permits correspondence bonuses only from unused materials.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow bonuses from materials generally; dial: restrict correspondence bonuses to unused materials to make magic rarer and harder, since the stricter rule narrows usable components.

rules.statement: After a year of steady use as a magical focus, an item gives +1 to spells related to its category of magic; the bonus rises to +2 after 10 years, +3 after 50, +4 after 100, +5 after 500, and +6 after 1,000 years, then increases by +1 for each further 500 years. The GM may also increase the Power of enchanted items through long use.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: steady use gradually strengthens a focus; dial: decide whether this accumulation also boosts enchanted-item Power, making old artifacts more potent.

rules.statement: A specially designed building grants a bonus to relevant spells cast from within it or into it, equal to the lower of the designer’s success margins in Architecture and Thaumatology. Designs covering multiple colleges grant half the smallest margin, rounded down; broader designs grant one-third, rounded down. A building may instead impose corresponding penalties by repelling magic.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: designed buildings channel or repel specified magical forces; dial: the GM can impose expense, awkward use, unusual siting, limited affected rooms, or disruption from later alterations.

rules.statement: When modifiers apply to enchantment, use those relevant to the spell being put into the item, not modifiers for the enchantment procedure itself. Inappropriate materials impose triple the usual penalty; modifiers to the enchanter’s skill affect the item’s Power, but do not modify spells cast with it.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Modifiers and Magic Items, p. 90 (gurps-thaumatology#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply spell-specific modifiers during creation; dial: none stated, while mismatched materials carry a severe transmission penalty.

rules.statement: A material’s inherent magic may be released through an appropriate skill and procedure; the substance can instead supply energy or reduce a spell’s energy cost, generally at one energy point per FP. Such material energy can be used when the caster has no FP and can enable solo casting that would otherwise need a ceremonial group.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Releasing Inherent Magic / Raw Energy, p. 97 (gurps-thaumatology#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow suitable materials to provide energy; dial: require potent materials to be consumed, and a failed casting may waste value or destroy them on a critical failure.

rules.statement: If a material is included rather than sacrificed, a failed casting usually leaves it intact, though it may need recovery or repair. The GM may reduce its energy value by about 10% after each failure; a critical failure may destroy it.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: included materials survive ordinary failures; dial: apply 10% value loss per failure or destruction on critical failure to make material power costly.

rules.statement: A prepared tree piece can serve as a one-use talisman spell for qualified users. After five minutes of preparation, the casting roll is 12 + Magery, reduced by 1 for each full day since cutting; success consumes the talisman, though maintained continuing spells persist.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Celtic Tree Talismans, p. 98 (gurps-thaumatology#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: successful use consumes the prepared piece; dial: freshness limits the casting roll, so delay weakens the talisman.

rules.statement: A spirit casts through the mortal after a contract is made; at casting, spirit aid can pay up to three times the higher of the caster’s Occultism or Thaumatology skill in energy, with the mortal paying any remainder. Spirit-assisted casting takes at least two seconds or the spell’s normal casting time, whichever is longer; ceremonial casting without spell knowledge takes at least one minute.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Concept; The Casting, pp. 91-92 (gurps-thaumatology#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: contracted spirits supply energy and cast through the mortal; dial: the assistance is capped by skill and creates a spiritual price, while the contract and summoning are prerequisites.

rules.statement: Spell modifiers are halved, rounded down, when used with spirit-assisted magic, while penalties retain their full value. The spirit’s energy contribution is applied before any energy-cost reduction from high skill.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: halve bonuses but not penalties because spiritual influence disrupts or taints resonances; the ordering of energy reductions limits the benefit.

rules.statement: At the end of a day when the wizard uses spirit-provided energy or a spell learned at reduced difficulty, he rolls Will + Magery, penalized by all energy borrowed since the previous test. Failure adds one level of Spiritual Distortion per 10 points or fraction of failure; distortion penalizes independently cast spells, and at 10 levels transforms the wizard and adds spiritual-energy addiction.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Price of Power; Long-Term Consequences, pp. 93-95 (gurps-thaumatology#010)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: borrowed power risks accumulating soul-warping distortion; dial: the GM may call for additional tests, while reaching the cap brings lasting changes and dependency.

rules.statement: Raw materials that provide 1 energy point or +1 to a skill roll cost about 1/250 of average starting wealth; at TL3, that is $4. As an optional scarcity limit, each casting may use only one indivisible external source, and a source’s cost doubles for every energy point beyond the first (so 2 points cost $8 and 10 cost $2,048).
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: price material energy at about $4 per point at TL3; dial: restrict each casting to one indivisible source with exponentially rising cost, because abundant cheap sources can enable overwhelming spells.

rules.statement: A correctly identified, extracted, and processed mana organ can temporarily serve a wizard in a similar way to its creature’s magical organ, or it can be consumed as a one-use energy source. Acquiring one may require a dangerous hunt, avoiding damage to a particular body part, and skilled preservation.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: allow temporary use or one-use energy from a properly prepared organ; dial: make acquisition and preservation difficult, because magical parts are hazardous and may be damaged.

rules.statement: Prepared dragon’s blood supplies 10 energy points per ounce for Fire magic only; it cannot fuel anti-fire spells, and use leaves an ashy, oily residue. The preparation may require an hour or two of work and a successful Alchemy roll.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Example: Dragon’s Blood, p. 100 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one ounce provides 10 points for Fire magic; dial: restrict the eligible magic and consume the material, because the potent supply is rare and costly.

rules.statement: A dose of atomized dragon’s blood fills about 2,000 cubic feet; any magic triggered in that space critically fails, including effects that normally need no roll. Disrupting any magic burns away the cloud and ends its effect.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Example: Dragon’s Blood—Wild Magic, p. 100 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: magic fails inside the cloud until a magical effect triggers; dial: the cloud ends upon disrupting magic, because that disruption consumes it.

rules.statement: A binary elixir is a distinct invention for a particular combination and delivery method. Inventing one also requires a successful Physician or suitable Esoteric Medicine roll; making it takes 25% longer and incurs an additional -2 to skill compared with the standard version.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Consuming Multiple Elixirs—Binary Elixirs, p. 106 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require a medical-skill roll and impose -2 and 25% extra production time; dial: vary the combination and method, because each distinct pairing must be developed separately.

rules.statement: Taking multiple elixirs in succession is normally safe. As an optional restriction, doses taken too close together—or while another is still active—may negate one another or produce altered effects, including changes in duration, sickness, or injury; a Body Control roll at about -3 may lessen the worst consequences.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Consuming Multiple Elixirs—Ad Hoc Mixing, p. 106 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: successive doses are safe; dial: make overlapping doses interfere or cause harmful mixtures, because their bodily transformations may react unpredictably.

rules.statement: A targeted alchemical treatment requires 3d minutes of analysis with Esoteric Medicine, followed by 1d+1 hours, a laboratory, supplies, and an Alchemy or Herb Lore roll to prepare it. Apply the margin of success as a bonus to the patient’s relevant HT or Body Control roll, with a minimum bonus of +2; critical success makes recovery automatic and immediately restores 1d lost HP and 1d lost attribute levels.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Alchemy and Medicine—Alchemical Cures, p. 106 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preparation grants at least +2 to recovery resistance; dial: require diagnosis, time, supplies, and a laboratory, because treatment must be tailored to the condition.

rules.statement: When treating the same condition in multiple patients at once, apply -1 to the preparation roll and add 10% to the required time for each patient after the first. A critical failure gives the patient -2 on their next two HT or Body Control rolls.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Alchemy and Medicine—Alchemical Cures, p. 106 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each additional patient makes batch treatment slower and less reliable; dial: use the critical-failure penalty, because an unsuitable preparation can worsen recovery.

rules.statement: An optional “kill or cure” rule makes a treated patient who fails an HT roll suffer 1d-3 injury, minimum 1; any failed preparation roll gives -1 on the patient’s next HT-based roll, and a critical failure also causes 1d-1 injury, minimum 1. A harsher option makes every treatment cause 1d-2 injury, minimum 0, unless the recipient succeeds at an HT roll, and leaves the patient nauseated for 3d minutes.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Alchemy and Medicine—“Kill or Cure,” p. 108 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: treatment has no stated extra injury risk; dial: apply one of the optional harm profiles, because powerful infusions may overstress the patient’s body.

rules.statement: Special ingredients associated with an elixir’s effect may give a bonus to Alchemy when available in sufficient quantity, or reduce expenses by replacing costly ordinary materials. Herbal preparations should cost at least 50% less in materials than alchemical ones, up to a maximum discount of $100.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Alchemy and Special Modifiers, p. 102; Herb Lore—Costs, p. 104 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: suitable rare ingredients can improve skill or lower expense, while herbal materials are cheaper; dial: vary bonuses and savings by ingredient and preparation, because effects depend on what is available and how it is processed.

rules.statement: Quick Gadgeteer allows a known preparation to be made in minutes equal to half its normal time in days, rounded up. The Alchemy roll takes the elixir’s full default penalty, any penalty for lacking a formulary or supervision, and an extra -1 for improvised equipment; ingredient costs do not change.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Alchemical Gadgeteering—Quick Gadgeteering, p. 103 (gurps-thaumatology#011)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: quick production retains ingredient costs and adds an equipment penalty; dial: reduce time at the cost of a harder roll, because rushed preparation relies on improvised methods.

rules.statement: Delivery method sets an elixir’s onset: examples range from 1d×5 minutes for a potion, to 1d seconds for injection, with other forms taking seconds to an hour. Aerosols cost twice the usual production cost, and the GM decides which elixirs can use each form.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Elixir Delivery Methods, p. 107 (gurps-thaumatology#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: delivery controls onset; dial: choose slower or faster forms and their cost; the in-world reason is how the preparation is administered.

rules.statement: An item can only receive a spell if it is normally eligible for item enchantment; the GM may allow other spells and sets their energy cost by comparison with similar spells. The spell’s form can be adapted to the setting’s materials, while copied magical scroll-files may be inert or may share a charge that is spent when any copy is triggered.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Standard System, p. 107 (gurps-thaumatology#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use spells normally eligible for items; dial: allow other effects or different copy behavior; the in-world limits are magical compatibility and the medium’s nature.

rules.statement: The GM can make Quick and Dirty enchantment harder, restrict collaboration, or remove one of the two standard methods. Slow and Sure can be made faster by allowing each participant to contribute energy equal to Magery per day, with a minimum of 1; a Magery 3 maker and Magery 2 assistant can then supply 100 energy in 20 days.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Quick and Dirty vs. Slow and Sure, pp. 108-109; p. 110 (gurps-thaumatology#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: retain the standard methods; dial: adjust speed, energy supply, and collaboration; the in-world constraint is the availability of time, helpers, and power.

rules.statement: A maker may convert an advantage, attribute, skill, or voluntarily assumed disadvantage into enchantment energy, if the GM approves a trait relevant to the work. Each character point yields 25 energy; with Slow and Sure, each five character points or fraction also takes one day instead of the usual day per energy point, and the sacrificed trait may be permanently lost.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Spending of Yourself, pp. 109, 111 (gurps-thaumatology#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: personal traits can be spent for item energy; dial: permit recovery or permanent loss; the in-world cost is surrendering part of oneself.

rules.statement: An item may gain 1 energy point per year in normal mana if it remains in qualifying circumstances; the rate is halved in low mana, doubled in high mana, tripled in very high mana, and negligible below low mana. Significance or practical use can also qualify an item, and the GM chooses what powers develop.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Enchantment through Age: Mechanisms and Rate of Enchantment, pp. 110-112 (gurps-thaumatology#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: qualifying items slowly accumulate power; dial: vary the rate and qualifying circumstances; the in-world source is ambient mana, significance, or use.

rules.statement: A noteworthy deed can add energy to an item: a significant killing may yield 20%–100% of the victim’s character-point value, with 100% recommended, while an ordinary killing or theft may yield nothing. The GM judges other deeds and assigns the resulting enchantment; divide energy by 25 when converting it to character points.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Enchantment through Deeds, pp. 112-113 (gurps-thaumatology#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: noteworthy deeds can empower objects; dial: set the award and what counts as noteworthy; the in-world cause is the deed’s significance and associated emotion.

rules.statement: A traumatic event can imbue an item with energy in proportion to the life force or emotion involved; an owner’s death may yield 20%–100% of their character-point total. For an extraordinary event, a participant may try a Will roll at -5 to trigger the process if the scene is roleplayed appropriately.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: exceptional trauma can leave power in an object; dial: determine the energy and whether a deliberate attempt is allowed; the in-world cost or source is death, determination, or intense emotion.

rules.statement: An item may be built as an advantage with gadget limits; making it can take 200 hours per character point, or use a skill roll whose failure wastes the effort. On success, the item does not function until its first owner pays character points equal to its modified advantage cost to attune it.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Magic Items as Advantages, p. 113 (gurps-thaumatology#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an advantage-item requires substantial manufacture and owner attunement; dial: use the time-based or skill-roll method; the in-world cost is labor and the owner’s points.

rules.statement: Appropriate visible design features can reduce an enchantment’s energy cost by 2% each, or by 1% when the symbolism requires close inspection or specialist knowledge; the usual maximum reduction is about 10%–15%. Misleading features instead add 5% energy each and may impose a cumulative -1 skill penalty per feature.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Resonant Designs and Materials, p. 111 (gurps-thaumatology#012)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apt symbolism reduces energy cost and misleading symbolism raises it; dial: adjust the permitted discount and penalties; the in-world cause is the design’s magical correspondence.

rules.statement: An item’s activation may require fuel, a skill roll, special circumstances, or a dangerous sacrifice instead of FP; the GM sets the requirement to suit the item’s power. Requirements that make an item unusable or let it overshadow character abilities should be avoided.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: activation can have item-specific conditions or costs; dial: set how demanding they are; the in-world limit is the item’s peculiar operating requirement.

rules.statement: A magic weapon’s attack is tied to the physical item: it can be taken from its user, damaged, or rendered ineffective by low mana when the attack has that limitation. In the example, the sword has DR 12, is uniquely made, and its attacks can affect insubstantial targets and penetrate half DR.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: keep item abilities attached to an object; dial: reduce breakability, theft, or mana limits if dependable gear is desired; the in-world cost is a vulnerable or unusually powerful artifact.

rules.statement: A rubbed lamp summons a bound djinni that must fulfill wishes as well as it can; the example’s summon appears on 15 or less, but may be subject to arcane restrictions, and the djinni’s abilities may still be limited by mana.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: make the summoned being obligated but not perfectly reliable; dial: remove restrictions or mana limits for greater access; the in-world cost is binding an unwilling, powerful spirit.

rules.statement: A gadget’s owner may purchase a Talent associated with the device’s abilities, usually at 5 points per level unless the device is exceptionally versatile. If the item is lost, the Talent has no value.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Power Talents and Gadget Items, p. 115 (gurps-thaumatology#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: skill benefits depend on continued access to the gadget; dial: allow the Talent to remain useful without it for a more portable benefit; the in-world cost is reliance on the device.

rules.statement: An item’s built-in restrictions can limit how it is used, and enchantments can impose ongoing emotional influence or commands on someone holding or wearing it. A curse may also make an item impossible to put down, while concealed or subtle drawbacks can keep users relying on it.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Restricted Items and Cursed Items, p. 116 (gurps-thaumatology#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restrictions and compulsions constrain the bearer; dial: make the effects easier to notice or resist; the in-world cost is impaired choice and risk of misuse.

rules.statement: An item with IQ 1–5 is willful but cannot use language; at IQ 1 it pursues simple goals, while IQ 5 can understand the gist of speech and plan a few minutes ahead. At IQ 6 or higher it is sapient, self-aware, and potentially independent.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: IQ determines how independently an item can reason; dial: lower IQ for a more tool-like creation or raise it for an autonomous character; the in-world cost is the item’s potential to act on its own.

rules.statement: An item spirit’s Will may exceed its IQ, up to the template spirit’s original Will; each excess Will point adds 50 energy to the creation cost. A linking enchantment can make the item’s other enchantments function only with the spirit’s approval.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a stronger-willed spirit costs more to create and can gate the item’s other powers; dial: reduce the excess Will or omit the approval condition; the in-world cost is energy and loss of control.

rules.statement: A maker may deliberately invest some of their life force to make an item willful without spells; one suggested permanent sacrifice is 1 point of HT. Items with abilities that draw on energy can have FP reserves sized to their charge, with limited reserves represented by less FP.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Enchantment Through Time or Deeds; Attributes and Secondary Characteristics, pp. 117–118 (gurps-thaumatology#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: creation consumes a lasting personal resource or gives the item finite reserves; dial: reduce the sacrifice or enlarge reserves; the in-world cost is life force or stored energy.

rules.statement: An object that cannot move under its own power has Move 0 and receives no extra points for that fact; it cannot have movement-related body parts. If it has manipulators, stability-dependent tasks take -6 DX unless it is anchored to a person or vehicle at least ten times its mass.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a portable object has no self-propelled movement and suffers a handling penalty; dial: permit movement or reduce the penalty; the in-world cost is dependence on being carried or anchored.

rules.statement: In a no-mana area an enchanted item normally becomes mundane and resumes functioning when it returns to mana; an item-character with No-Mana Shutdown instead becomes comatose there. This trait costs -20 points, while an item that deteriorates there uses a different dependency limitation.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no mana disables the item’s supernatural function; dial: remove shutdown or use mere power loss instead; the in-world cost is possible indefinite incapacitation in a hostile zone.

rules.statement: A weapon-form entity with an attack that must be wielded cannot use that attack itself and requires dedicated control; the wielder supplies the relevant weapon skill and, for a melee attack, their ST is used. A version that can also attack independently costs +20%, while mana-dependent attacks can be limited to require mana.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the attack requires a cooperating wielder; dial: allow self-use at an added cost; the in-world cost is dependence on a user and their physical strength.

rules.statement: Path/Book rituals are performed as extended Concentrate maneuvers; when attacked or injured, the caster must pass Will-3 to continue, and disruption of the equipment or ritual space can stop the casting. Under Effect Shaping, the ceremony has a more-or-less fixed procedure and works only if correctly performed and resistance is overcome.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Effect Shaping Theory; Path/Book Magic in Operation, pp. 122, 125 (gurps-thaumatology#013)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rituals require time, concentration, and an intact working space; dial: reduce those requirements for more immediate magic; the in-world cost is vulnerability during preparation.

rules.statement: Each level of Path/Book Adept, up to three, lets the magician omit one ritual element chosen when the advantage is bought. It can instead reduce the time element to 1d seconds of concentration; further shortening under Effect Shaping requires accepting a skill penalty.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: faster or element-free rituals require a costly specialized advantage; dial: permit more rapid casting or flexible element choice; the in-world cost is exceptional training and prerequisites.

rules.statement: If ritual magic draws on the divine hierarchy, sanctity can modify ritual skill: no sanctity gives at least -5 and may make rituals ineffective; low sanctity requires single-use preparation and gives -1 (or -3 to adepts); high sanctity gives +1 to +3, and very high gives +4 or +5 when invoked powers are mutually friendly. Opposed religious alignments can reverse these effects.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Ritual Space and Sanctity, p. 126 (gurps-thaumatology#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: sanctity may be unrelated; dial: link it to ritual space; the in-world cause is whether local powers welcome or oppose the invocation.

rules.statement: If ritual magic uses mana in place of ritual space, no mana prevents results; low mana imposes -5 and restricts rituals to suitably gifted magicians; normal mana permits normal use by mages (optionally, non-mages at -5); high or very high mana permits anyone to work rituals.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Ritual Space and Mana, p. 126 (gurps-thaumatology#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use ritual space rather than mana; dial: make local mana govern access and skill; the in-world cost is dependence on a sufficiently active magical environment.

rules.statement: Suitable ritual elements can add skill bonuses, but their combined bonuses cannot exceed +15. Omitting elements usually penalizes the roll, with no upper limit on the cumulative penalty; adepts can omit elements and remain effective.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: elements focus intent and may improve results; dial: change the +15 ceiling; the cost of shortcuts is increased risk of failure or backfire.

rules.statement: In Effect Shaping, a ritual usually takes 10 minutes to an hour and resolves at the end. Taking three times the basic time or longer gives +1; a multi-day preparation gives +1 for a two-day total period, with another +1 each time that period doubles, but missed preparation days waste prior work.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Time; Extra Time, p. 127 (gurps-thaumatology#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the listed duration and modifiers; dial: make careful, repeated preparation grant further bonuses; the cost is time, uninterrupted work, and protecting the site.

rules.statement: No prepared ritual space gives -5; a successful 1d-minute preparation of a room-sized area reduces this to -1 for the next ritual, while at least an hour of daily preparation for a week removes the penalty indefinitely. A site used for 20, 50, 100, 500, or 1,000 years gains +1, +2, +3, +4, or +5 respectively; the GM determines how quickly its bonus decays if neglected.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: preparation and long use improve a location; dial: set decay for abandoned sites; the in-world cost is sustained care and time spent consecrating it.

rules.statement: A subject lacking any name, title, or nickname usually imposes at least -5 and may be impossible to target. A clearly defined group can be targeted at -2; an unclear group generally gives -5 unless the caster knows each member’s personal name.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Material and Symbolic Components—Names, pp. 128–130 (gurps-thaumatology#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a name or precise description helps establish the target; dial: make missing identification more or less punishing; the in-world limit is difficulty connecting the ritual to an indistinct subject.

rules.statement: An area-targeted ritual uses area modifiers and requires the caster to define its boundaries; it may affect those inside, those who enter while it lasts, or those who perform a specified activity there. A ritual aimed at a group instead uses multiple-target modifiers and generally needs representations of the group.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Multiple Targets; Area, pp. 130–132 (gurps-thaumatology#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: apply scope penalties and require boundaries or group definition; dial: adjust feasibility for very large targets; the in-world cost is greater difficulty and suitable symbolic connections.

rules.statement: A continuing or conditional effect needs a stated duration. A triggered ritual is rolled once after casting penalties are set and again when its trigger occurs, using the same skill; applicable resistance contests the trigger roll, and a critical failure makes the effect fail for 1d weeks or end it if its duration expires first.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Duration; Triggering an Effect, p. 131 (gurps-thaumatology#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: set the duration and test both creation and activation; dial: change the critical-failure consequence; the in-world limit is that stored magic can falter when called upon.

rules.statement: A ritual’s subject can usually resist with Will, with Magic Resistance adding to the resistance roll; the caster’s modified skill and the subject’s resistance are compared. For group targets, use the most difficult member for penalties and make one resistance roll using the group’s best applicable defense; even a successful ritual may affect only part of a sufficiently large group, according to the caster’s margin of success.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Group Defenses and Resistance; Number Affected, pp. 130–131 (gurps-thaumatology#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: subjects instinctively oppose an unknown ritual, and group defenses constrain its reach; dial: alter resistance or affected-count assumptions; the in-world cost is stronger protection and reduced reliability against diverse groups.

rules.statement: In high-powered collaboration, divide ritual-parameter penalties among the magicians, rounding against them, but apply each caster’s ritual-element penalties and bonuses individually and impose -1 per additional magician. Everyone rolls; any failure ruins the ritual, while successes combine their margins, and resistible effects use the group’s average modified skill plus +1 per extra caster.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Combined Efforts—High-Powered Collaboration, pp. 132–134 (gurps-thaumatology#014)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: skilled magicians can share parameter burdens; dial: choose the collaboration model; the in-world costs are coordination, added penalties, and shared consequences from failure.

rules.statement: Casting across dimensional boundaries gives -10 per boundary, reduced to -5 at places where planes intersect. These penalties do not apply to rituals whose purpose is to open portals, contact other realms, or summon beings from beyond the caster’s dimension.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: crossing boundaries makes ordinary rituals harder; dial: change penalties or exempt other cross-boundary effects; the in-world cost is separation between dimensions.

rules.statement: A ritual may be set to begin when a stated trigger occurs during its specified duration, or to end early when a stated condition is met. It must have enough energy or suitable ritual elements for the eventual target; excess resistance beyond what was allowed prevents the effect.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects start after the ceremony and last for their set duration; dial: triggers and early-ending conditions; the caster must budget for likely targets and defenses.

rules.statement: A caster may combine rituals if they share the same target and, when relevant, the same energy aspect. In energy-accumulating work, the casters’ gathered energy pays the combined cost; each resisted effect is opposed separately.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rituals are separate; dial: combine compatible effects; the shared target and energy aspect constrain combinations.

rules.statement: A magician can normally end their own ongoing ritual by concentrating for 1d−2 seconds, minimum 1, without a roll. They cannot do so if it has run wild, has confusing aspected effects, or is otherwise beyond their control.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Canceling and Dispelling Effects, p. 138 (gurps-thaumatology#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ongoing effects run their stated course; dial: the caster may end controllable workings; loss of control removes this option.

rules.statement: Breaking an object that carries a ritual effect often ends that effect; destroying a malefice without magic typically cancels the hostile working tied to it.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Canceling and Dispelling Effects, p. 138; Path/Book-Related Items, p. 139 (gurps-thaumatology#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects persist until their duration ends; dial: make a physical object a point of failure; the object must be found and broken.

rules.statement: A person may carry or use only one charm made by a particular ritual at a time, and a charm usually works only for its intended recipient. A charm can be prepared beforehand and made to activate when handled or used, if its ritual permits.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: charms are recipient-specific and limited to one per ritual type; dial: allow activation by a trigger; access and carrying capacity limit use.

rules.statement: In energy-accumulating magic, an aged artifact can provide one ritual energy point once per casting for each 100 energy points, or 4 character points, invested in it through long use. A variant powerstone approach instead converts each 5 points it would provide into 1 ritual energy point.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: energy must be accumulated externally; dial: an item supplies a limited amount per casting; creating such items is generally difficult or requires a bound spirit or centuries of use.

rules.statement: An ongoing effect with a starting condition activates when that condition occurs during its set duration; a conditional ending can lift it sooner. A curse tied to an oath, for example, may take effect when the oath is broken.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: no oath-triggered consequence; dial: attach a curse to breach of terms; its duration and the caster’s estimate of possible targets constrain it.

rules.statement: A ritual can alter or erase one selected memory if the subject fails to resist; the subject may later recover or reconstruct it through specified mental methods, with a penalty equal to the caster’s margin of victory. Otherwise, the change is permanent.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Path of Cunning: Cloud Memory, p. 140 (gurps-thaumatology#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: memories remain intact; dial: remove or replace one memory; recovery is harder by the degree of the caster’s success.

rules.statement: A ritual can make its subject look and sound like another person, including their clothing, for its duration, but does not change abilities. Observers do not resist the effect, and it remains visible in photographs and video.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Path of Cunning: Guise, p. 140 (gurps-thaumatology#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: appearance is unchanged; dial: alter appearance and clothing; identity is only a visible-and-audible disguise, not a change of abilities.

rules.statement: A ritual can plant one command in a resisting subject’s mind; when it is triggered, the subject rolls Will at a penalty equal to the caster’s margin of victory, and on failure carries it out as best they can. Dangerous, bizarre, or strongly out-of-character orders may make resistance easier.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The Path of Cunning: Suggestion, p. 140 (gurps-thaumatology#015)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the subject chooses their actions; dial: install one later-triggered command; the subject can still resist when it activates.

rules.statement: Night Terrors costs 10 energy points and takes 1 hour to cast. The subject resists normally; when they next sleep, their body becomes rigid for a nightmare lasting 1d minutes, and waking early requires a Will roll at -6. Afterwards they make a Fright Check at a penalty of twice the caster’s margin of victory; repeated successful castings on consecutive days add -1 per day, but multiple castings in one day cause only one attack, and the subject must spend a day awake before being attacked again.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one nightmare at the next sleep; dial: consecutive days worsen the Fright Check; the cost is repeated exposure and a day awake between attacks.

rules.statement: Slumber costs 4 energy points and takes 10 minutes. The target resists with Will, penalized by twice the FP lost to missed sleep or Nightmares; on a successful resistance they still roll every 2 hours at the same penalty until they fall asleep. The effect causes natural sleep, with a minimum of 1d hours if undisturbed, and the subject can be awakened normally.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a one-off inclination to sleep with no duration adjustment; dial: missed sleep increases the resistance penalty; the cost is vulnerability to being put to sleep.

rules.statement: Calm the Winds costs 2 energy points plus 1 per level of wind reduction and takes 10 minutes to cast over an area. Each level reduces wind by one Beaufort step; the reduction equals the caster’s margin of success, with at least 1 level of effect. Wind-driven waves may also lessen, but the effect cannot stop a large wave merely by calming a small patch of air.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Calm the Winds, p. 142 (gurps-thaumatology#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the cast covers an area and reduces wind by at least one step; dial: each additional step costs another energy point; the cost is paid to calm a region, not to cancel every consequence of a storm.

rules.statement: Command the Waves costs 6 energy points plus 1 per effectiveness level and takes 10 minutes to cast over an area. Each level raises or lowers wave height by 1 foot, with at least 1 level; at 5 levels, floating objects can be moved through the area at 1 yard per second in any direction.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Command the Waves, p. 142 (gurps-thaumatology#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: at least 1 level of wave change; dial: greater change costs 1 more energy point per level; the effect is confined to the cast area.

rules.statement: Thunderbolt costs 12 energy points and is performed in two stages: preparing a charm and then completing the strike within 12 hours, unless the caster accepts extended-duration modifiers. The charm must be placed on or near the target; the completed ritual calls down lightning, which cannot be dodged if the charm is on the target and destroys the charm on success. In the energy-accumulating method, one-third of the energy is spent preparing the charm and the remaining two-thirds on the strike.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the charm enables a single strike within 12 hours; dial: delay can be extended at a penalty or extra cost; the charm is consumed by a successful strike.

rules.statement: Reversion of Form costs 9 energy points and takes 30 minutes. It forces a transformed subject back into their true form; a magical transformation resists, while a subject changed by an innate ability can resist with the better of HT or Will, plus applicable Talent. A momentary casting changes the subject once, while a longer duration keeps them in their native form for that duration.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Reversion of Form, p. 144 (gurps-thaumatology#016)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a one-time return to the subject’s true form; dial: a longer duration prevents another transformation for longer; the target may resist according to the source of the change.

rules.statement: Skinchange costs 9 energy points and takes 20 minutes, adjusted by the animal form’s template: for each 10 character points or fraction by which that template exceeds the caster’s racial template, the energy-accumulating cost rises by 1. Success immediately gives the caster that animal form for the effect’s duration or until the effect is negated; some traditions require a prepared animal skin, and many do not allow casting it on someone else.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the caster takes one species-specific animal form; dial: more costly templates raise the energy requirement; the transformation lasts only while its effect holds.

rules.statement: Fix Glitch costs 4 energy points and takes 10 minutes. It repairs minor problems in one machine when the necessary work could be done with that machine’s standard tool kit, no replacement parts, and no more than 30 minutes of ordinary work; the repair starts after casting and takes half the usual time. The machine must be accessible to standard tools, so a locked casing requires its key.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repair is limited to minor work on one machine and uses no replacement parts; dial: none specified; access to the machine and its tools is the practical constraint.

rules.statement: Fuel costs 6 energy points and takes 10 minutes. It supplies enough fuel, charge, or reaction mass for one nonmagically powered mundane machine to run at full power and normal efficiency for 1 hour; the supplied fuel cannot be taken out for use elsewhere, and if extracted it does not work.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one machine receives a 1-hour supply; dial: none specified; the fuel is bound to that machine and cannot be repurposed.

rules.statement: Evil Eye costs 12 energy points and takes 1 hour to cast on the magician, who can then make one lethal attack by making eye contact with a target within the effect’s duration, which can be no longer than a day. The two contest Will; if the caster wins, the target makes a HT roll penalized by the caster’s ritual margin of success, while a caster who loses suffers the same effects as the target would. A tie normally wastes the attack.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one attack within at most a day, with a reciprocal risk if the caster loses the contest; dial: the caster’s success margin sets the target’s HT penalty; the cost is potential harm to the attacker.

rules.statement: On success, the caster’s spirit leaves the body and can travel while intangible for the ritual’s duration; the body is comatose and has no resistance to possession. If the spirit remains away after the effect ends, both spirit and body immediately lose 1d-3 HP, then 1 HP every 12 hours until they reunite or one dies; this damage cannot be healed before reunion.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spirit returns when the effect ends; dial: travel and return conditions; the abandoned body is vulnerable and both halves suffer escalating harm if separated.

rules.statement: A spirit resists with Will; if the caster wins, the spirit must carry out a number of commanded tasks equal to the caster’s margin of victory. A task is a short combat action or one longer action otherwise, and the caster must specify any spirit powers needed; an impossible instruction is ignored.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spirit can resist and only a limited number of tasks can be imposed; dial: task scope and spirit availability; the binding cannot supply powers or energy the spirit lacks.

rules.statement: The ritual gives a present spirit a physical body assembled from suitable materials; the body’s abilities depend on its construction and the ritual’s success. When the effect ends, the body falls apart or reverts, and if the spirit is driven out or crosses a spirit-blocking barrier, the body becomes lifeless.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the constructed body lasts only for the effect; dial: materials, abilities, and duration; specialized ingredients and crafting may be costly or dangerous.

rules.statement: A Ward penalizes hostile rituals crossing its boundary by its Power and makes supernatural beings roll to cross, with a penalty equal to that Power. Spirits can spend FP equal to the Ward’s initial Power to lower its Power by 1 for themselves; enough spirits doing so can lower it for everyone, while physical supernatural beings can also degrade it through accumulated thrust damage.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the boundary blocks hostile crossings but can be weakened; dial: Power and permitted entities; maintaining or breaching it demands resources, and it cannot be replaced until removed or eliminated.

rules.statement: Doom produces a staged curse: nightmares begin the following night, material misfortune starts within a week, and a final accident or violence follows 1d days later, inflicting damage equal to three times the success margin, minimum 3d, before the curse ends. The victim may resist with Will, while protection against it works at -4; killing the caster or persuading the caster to lift it ends the curse, but lifting it transfers the effects to the client.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the harm unfolds in stages and ends after its final blow; dial: severity and resistance; the curse risks backlash for its caster and gives the victim opportunities to seek help.

rules.statement: Curse Mirror contests its roll against the first hostile curse aimed at its subject; if it wins, the attacker suffers that curse instead. If placed on a charm, the charm breaks when triggered whether or not it wins, and its bearer knows whether the defense was penetrated.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: it answers only the first curse and must win a contest; dial: whether it protects a person or a charm; a charm is consumed by the attempt.

rules.statement: A successful vision of luck answers a question about the consequences of a proposed action, usually in one or two words; greater success may add detail. The GM chooses a reasonable answer and may make minor changes to the plot or setting so it proves accurate.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Vision of Luck, p. 152 (gurps-thaumatology#017)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the answer is vague and concerns a proposed course of action; dial: the amount of detail; foreknowledge is limited and may prompt the client to avoid the ritual.

rules.statement: Loyal Item makes a single item return to its owner through a chain of chance events, potentially taking hours for a small object in a city or weeks or months for a large or isolated one. A finder holding an appealing or valuable item resists with Will, rerolling weekly; the effect ends if the owner willingly gives the item away, and a ward can trap it unless the ritual wins a contest to leave.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: chance eventually draws the item back; dial: return time and duration; distance, size, isolation, possessors, and wards can delay or stop its return.

rules.statement: Weatherworking affects an area one mile across, with each -1 to skill and +1 energy increasing its diameter by another mile. The caster adds the success margin to the chance that the requested weather occurs naturally; on success, it arrives within 12 hours unless the caster pays -1 skill and +1 energy per hour or, after one hour, per minute of reduced onset.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: requested weather must still pass a probability check and fades according to local conditions; dial: area and onset speed; forcing unlikely weather or rapid change costs more.

rules.statement: Dispel Ritual contests the target effect’s effective skill, or the original caster’s Will if that caster is linked to or aware of the attempt; success ends the effect, while a tie or loss has no effect. Out-of-control effects require three successful attempts, each reducing their power by a third, and failures can cause mental or physical harm.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: removal requires winning a contest; dial: resistant or out-of-control effects may take multiple attempts; failure can expose the dispeller to magical feedback.

rules.statement: A Chaperone charm automatically prevents the wearer’s next significant danger, including a threat that could cause death or disabling injury; it automatically defeats minor curses, but only delays a major curse for 1d days. The charm breaks after acting, and a person cannot benefit from more than one at a time.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: it stops one significant danger and is then spent; dial: the caster may specify a threat category; the one-charm limit prevents stockpiling protection.

rules.statement: The ritual can alter a spirit’s traits to fit a constructed body, but the net value of the changes—excluding its immateriality and invisibility traits—cannot exceed 10 points per point of ritual success margin. The spirit need not enter the body; if multiple suitable spirits compete, they make a Quick Contest of Wills, with the intended spirit potentially receiving +1 to +3.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cap body-related gains by the ritual margin; dial: the GM negotiates which traits fit the materials and concept, because the body’s construction defines its capabilities.

rules.statement: Empower transfers FP to a spirit: under Effect Shaping, the amount is five times the success margin, with a minimum of 5 FP; under Energy Accumulating, it costs 6 energy plus 1 per 5 FP transferred. FP above the spirit’s normal total dissipates after 1d seconds, and confinement rituals between caster and spirit resist the transfer.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: excess FP lasts only 1d seconds; dial: the GM decides whether a magic item supplies suitable energy, since the source must match the spirit’s needs.

rules.statement: Exorcise makes approaching a protected person or area painful; a living subject also carries protection extending Will/3 yards, rounded down. A spirit resists with Will-5: success imposes -1 to DX and IQ while it remains there, while failure repels it, and a critical success by the caster or critical failure by the spirit makes the repulsion permanent; a spirit already present must leave any possessed body or living host behind.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resistance determines whether the spirit is merely impaired or driven away; dial: the effect can become permanent only on the specified critical result.

rules.statement: Fetish binds a present spirit that is obedient to the caster, willingly or through coercion; its skill penalty or energy surcharge equals the higher of the spirit’s ST or HT. Failure frees the spirit from any compulsion to obey and makes later attempts on that spirit cumulatively harder or costlier by 1; critical failure prevents further attempts.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spirit must be present and obedient, and its physical strength or health raises the casting cost; dial: the GM may adjust that surcharge for the spirit.

rules.statement: A fetish lets its holder use the spirit’s eligible powers as if they were the spirit’s, and can also supply its FP to the holder’s supernatural abilities; the spirit’s FP fuels powers that require it, but the fetish stops working when the spirit reaches 0 FP. If the spirit supplies energy to an accumulating ritual, each 5 FP becomes 1 energy point.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: only eligible powers are available, and use ends when the spirit has no FP; dial: the GM may allow the spirit’s FP to power accumulating rituals.

rules.statement: A fetish used to maintain a permanent charm cannot also provide the spirit’s powers or FP to its holder. A critical failure while using a fetish’s powers, FP, or charm can let the spirit escape if it wins a Quick Contest of Wills against the holder; destroying the fetish frees the spirit, which then rolls HT or suffers stun and 1d damage, or 4d damage on a critical failure.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: permanent charm use precludes the fetish’s other functions and critical failure risks escape; dial: the GM can decide whether a freed spirit flees, attacks, or otherwise reacts.

rules.statement: Ghost Sword lets a weapon harm incorporeal spirits; it takes 30 minutes and is modified by -1 to skill or +1 energy per full 2 lbs. of weapon weight. It can affect ammunition but not the ranged weapon itself, does not grant the ability to see or detect spirits, and can overcome protective rituals through a Quick Contest when the magic is linked to spirits.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the weapon’s weight increases the difficulty or cost, and ranged enchantment applies to ammunition; dial: the GM determines which protective rituals qualify for the contest.

rules.statement: Lay to Rest permanently guides a newly deceased person’s spirit onward and resists attempts to summon or resurrect it; each full week since death imposes -1 to skill or +1 energy. A would-be summoner must win a Quick Contest against the ritual to contact the spirit at all.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect is permanent and blocks contact unless overcome in a contest; dial: the destination depends on what the afterlife means for that person.

rules.statement: Spirit Slave captures part of a living subject’s soul, who may resist with Will; preparations can impose -1 to -5 on that resistance. On failure, the subject gains High Pain Threshold and Hidebound and suffers -10 to Will when resisting the caster’s other rituals; while the caster holds the soul-container, attempts by others to affect the subject’s soul or spirit automatically fail, otherwise the subject resists those attempts at -10, and breaking the container ends the effect.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the soul-fragment’s container controls access and breaking it cancels the effect; dial: the GM may allow the victim’s ghost to remain under the caster’s control after death.

rules.statement: Spirit Trap imprisons a spirit in a closed container for the ritual’s duration if the caster wins a contest against the spirit’s higher Will or ST; breaking the container frees it. Summon requires the caster to know a unique spirit’s name or a spirit type, and a reluctant spirit resists with Will-3; on success it appears nearby and in sight, but may be unhelpful, while unwilling powerful spirits can impose a reaction penalty from -1 to -5.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Spirit Trap and Summon (p. 162) (gurps-thaumatology#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: capture depends on winning resistance and the container remaining intact; dial: the GM may vary ritual costs for spirit types and reactions to hostile summons.

rules.statement: Thicken the Walls of the World reinforces reality throughout its area for the effect’s duration, resisting attempts to summon extradimensional entities, open portals to other realms, or channel divine or diabolical power there. The GM determines the exact scope of what it blocks.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Thicken the Walls of the World (p. 165) (gurps-thaumatology#018)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the effect blocks the listed kinds of supernatural intrusion within its area; dial: the GM decides which other attempts count as affected.

rules.statement: A working normally combines two symbols, commonly an action and a target; complex or powerful effects may require more symbols or repeated symbols. The GM determines which symbols fit an intended effect, and greater complexity takes more time and creates more chances to fail because each symbol must be handled with a skill roll.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Working the Magic, p. 172 (gurps-thaumatology#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use the minimum symbols that represent the intended effect; dial: add symbols or repeats for complexity or potency, at the cost of time and more skill checks.

rules.statement: For each occurrence of each symbol, the caster must succeed at a roll against the lower of Symbol Drawing and that symbol’s skill to create or place it. Afterward, activation takes one second per symbol and uses a roll against the lowest of Symbol Drawing and any one involved symbol skill; the effect activates on success, even if earlier drawing failures left flaws, and a failed activation usually costs 1 FP while a critical failure has the full cost and a critical-failure result.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Drawing the Symbols and Activating the Symbols, pp. 172-174 (gurps-thaumatology#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: require separate preparation and activation checks and charge for failed activation; dial: allow more time for +1 or accept reduced time for -2, trading speed for reliability.

rules.statement: Activation cannot occur in no mana; in low mana it is at -5 and may require Magery, while normal or high mana has no activation penalty but may still require Magery. Very high mana reduces total energy cost, but any failure becomes a critical failure; in no mana, symbols cannot be drawn effectively either.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: mana conditions govern whether activation is possible and how risky it is; dial: make wild mana risky even during drawing, with critical failures causing dramatic misbehavior.

rules.statement: A parchment stores a defined effect and can be carried by anyone, but damage to any part makes it unusable; the user must understand its purpose, studying an unfamiliar one for 10 minutes per symbol and rolling at -1 per symbol after the first. Each person can keep one ready parchment plus one per two Symbol Drawing levels above IQ, and making or studying a new one displaces the oldest when over that limit.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Parchment Symbol Casting, pp. 173-174 (gurps-thaumatology#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a parchment is portable but fragile, limited in ready quantity, and may require study; dial: vary what materials can carry the symbols, with damage still ending their usefulness.

rules.statement: To activate a parchment, the user makes the usual activation roll, at -4 if someone else made it, and pays its energy cost on success. Whether the roll succeeds or fails, the parchment is consumed and its magic cannot be reused.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Parchment Symbol Casting, p. 175 (gurps-thaumatology#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: one use consumes the written effect; dial: use inscriptions in earth or sand for repeated activations, but they are immobile, easily damaged, and last at most the lesser of 3d hours or 2d uses.

rules.statement: Ordinary symbol tokens take at least one second per symbol to ready, and their activation takes three times the usual time and suffers -2 per token. Each caster must make their own tokens; replacing one takes 2, 6, 12, or 24 hours for Easy, Average, Hard, or Very Hard symbol skills.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reusable tokens offer flexibility at the cost of preparation time, activation delay, and skill penalties; dial: permit rushed random selection, but the eventual effect must use all drawn symbols.

rules.statement: In an emergency, tracing symbols in the air imposes -3 on each symbol-drawing roll and does not create a reusable item; each symbol takes 2, 6, 12, or 30 seconds for Easy, Average, Hard, or Very Hard skill. In low mana, the drawing penalty becomes -8 and each symbol costs 1 FP, and activation must follow immediately after tracing.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: improvised casting is fast to deploy but penalized and leaves no stored effect; dial: a setting may prohibit it or require a special glowing implement.

rules.statement: A marked object can hold a one-off instantaneous effect until a nearby, clearly defined trigger occurs. Successful activation leaves it waiting for a caster-chosen period, normally a day, and the caster pays the full cost then; each additional day of duration costs half the casting energy, while rushing the inscription to minutes or seconds imposes -2 or -4 on all rolls and doubles or triples energy cost.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the trigger is proximity-based and the effect is temporary; dial: allow a reasonable defined trigger and longer waiting time, at increasing energy cost.

rules.statement: For a multi-symbol working, base energy cost is normally the sum of the symbols’ base costs; control effects double the cost of the controlled target’s symbol, and radical transformations count the symbols for both starting and ending forms. The result is a Regular-effect cost for an SM 0 subject or an Area-effect base, scaled for larger targets or areas and increased proportionally for larger effects; maintained effects usually last a minute and can generally be continued for half the casting cost.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cost scales with symbols, scope, magnitude, and duration; dial: reduce cost by 1 FP per full 2 points of activation margin, or in high-magic settings replace energy costs with scope penalties.

rules.statement: A permanent symbol item may require an activation roll; if it does not, its lowest relevant skill sets its Power and must be at least 15, or 20 to function in low mana. Using an item normally costs energy when its effect would; a self-powered item needs an added power-related symbol, and a continuing effect lasts only while the user holds, wears, or occupies the item before needing reactivation.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: items either draw the user’s energy or need an added symbol to power themselves; dial: require activation or not, changing the skill that sets Power and the enchantment time.

rules.statement: A Word of Power costs 36 energy points, paid from FP and then HP, and cannot draw on external energy; if the speaker dies before paying enough, its utterance fades out. A spoken Word can produce up to 360 energy points’ worth of magic at skill 36 and Magery 10, often within earshot, but without a critical success the GM decides all details.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Words of Power, pp. 178-179 (gurps-thaumatology#019)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: extraordinary output exacts potentially lethal personal energy and is unpredictable; dial: allow some effects from an interrupted or aborted Word, but keep their practical value minimal.

rules.statement: In a word-based working, add the energy costs of every Word. Double the cost of nouns subject to complex control; for a radical transformation, add the verb cost to the costs of both forms, counting the same noun twice if it governs both.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Determining Base Energy Cost, p. 182 (gurps-thaumatology#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: combine the Words’ costs; dial: the GM may instead increase costs for especially broad Realm categories, reflecting how much magical scope they cover.

rules.statement: A Realm-based working usually costs twice the level of its highest Realm, plus the levels of any other Realms used; for example, Fire/3 with Time/1 costs 7 energy. The GM may raise that cost when Realms have few, very broad levels.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: calculate cost from Realm levels; dial: the GM can raise it for broad Realms, reflecting their wider reach.

rules.statement: A working’s parameters can be set in advance, imposing skill penalties or extra energy, or left to the casting’s margin of success. If several parameters depend on margin, apply the full margin to each separately; the caster need not use all the power rolled.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use one parameter-setting approach; dial: the GM chooses between predictability, extra cost or penalties, and variable results.

rules.statement: For ordinary ranged effects, range usually costs -1 skill per yard, or +1 energy per two full yards. If margin of success sets range, margins 0–6 reach touch, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, and 100 yards respectively; continue the same 2-5-10 progression for higher margins.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Range and Familiarity, p. 182 (gurps-thaumatology#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use range penalties or added energy; dial: the GM can use margin instead, trading predictable reach for a result that varies with the roll.

rules.statement: A temporary effect normally lasts one minute and can be maintained by paying half its casting cost for each additional interval. Alternatively, use -2 skill per extra duration interval; maintaining a temporary effect by skill rather than ongoing energy makes it end at its set time unless recast. Turning an instantaneous effect into an ongoing one gives -2 skill and a base duration of 10 seconds.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: pay ongoing energy or accept the duration penalty; dial: the GM sets the base interval, with maintenance energy or a fixed end limiting persistence.

rules.statement: For a circular area, multiply base energy cost by the radius in yards; the GM may lower this for subtle, large-scale effects or raise it for powerful ones. If using skill penalties instead, the suggested cost is -1 skill per two yards of radius. With margin-based area, treat the margin as a Size Modifier; success by 6 permits up to a 20-yard diameter.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Area of Effect, pp. 183–184 (gurps-thaumatology#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: area requires more energy; dial: the GM may instead impose skill difficulty or reduce the burden for subtle effects, reflecting the difficulty of shaping a field.

rules.statement: A damaging working at base energy cost produces 1d damage; each additional die usually multiplies the energy cost. Alternatively, each added die gives -3 skill, or margin of success produces 1d per 2 points or fraction thereof, with a margin of 0 producing 1d-2.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: buy more damage with energy; dial: the GM may use skill penalties or margin instead, making destructive output harder to guarantee.

rules.statement: A word-based working requires successful rolls against both its verb and noun skills. If more than two Words are used, roll against the lowest relevant verb and noun skills, at -1 per extra Word; a transformation instead requires three rolls, for the verb and the nouns governing its initial and final forms.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Working the Effect; Transformations, p. 187 (gurps-thaumatology#020)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each required Word must succeed; dial: extra Words lower the roll, reflecting the added complexity of combining magical instructions.

rules.statement: An extended working may use repeated rolls, adding their margins together and counting a margin of 0 as 1; a resistible target rolls once against the total. Each roll after the first can cost an extra 1 FP or the full working cost, and later rolls may also take a cumulative -1 or -2 skill penalty.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: repeated effort accumulates effect; dial: extra fatigue, energy expenditure, and rising penalties keep long rituals costly and risky.

rules.statement: Sending a ranged effect across each dimensional boundary usually costs -10 skill, +10 energy, or a required margin of 5 per boundary; halve these values where dimensions intersect. A portal to another dimension normally needs no range modifier or margin by itself, though reaching a particularly difficult otherworld may be harder.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: crossing dimensions adds a substantial cost or difficulty; dial: the GM can halve it at intersecting planes or raise the hurdle for hard-to-reach worlds.

rules.statement: Realm mastery is divided into levels that progressively unlock sensing, manipulation, creation, and eventually authority over the Realm. In the three-level scheme, level 1 detects and analyzes, level 2 manipulates or suppresses without wholly creating or erasing, and level 3 permits finite creation and destruction; permanent or powerful creations may need another Realm or raw magic.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: One to Three Levels: Basic Structures (gurps-thaumatology#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: three levels give a compact progression; dial: add or remove levels to make mastery a longer climb or bring high power within reach sooner.

rules.statement: In a six-level scheme, level 1 is passive sensing; level 2 allows limited control within natural bounds; level 3 allows local command, repair, simple creation, and some effects on other minds or bodies; level 4 grants broad authority and can negate lower-level workings of the same Realm; level 5 permits radical transformations and complex creation; level 6 can locally alter the Realm’s own nature, but only temporarily and at the GM’s discretion.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: More Levels: Lower and Higher Mysteries (gurps-thaumatology#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: use graded capabilities to distinguish mastery; dial: a sixth level is legendary and potentially dangerous, while more than six risks excessive complexity.

rules.statement: Transforming a target into something belonging to a different Realm requires a high level in the Realm describing its current state, plus enough power in the destination Realm to make at least minor creations—suggested as one level below the first requirement, or level 2, whichever is higher. The GM may add skill penalties or energy costs for especially radical changes, even when both states belong to one Realm.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: cross-Realm changes require substantial mastery on both sides; dial: increase penalties or energy costs for more radical transformations.

rules.statement: Realm magic generally needs at least level 2 to cause damage, and such low-level harm is usually localized and limited; level 3 or higher can make attacks more effective. Directly damaging something governed by a Realm requires moderate-to-high mastery, or a combined working with a destructive Realm; each level above that needed to damage the target can add +1 damage per die, or the GM may instead use armor divisor (2) or slower or incurable injury.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Realms and Damage; Enhanced Damage at High Levels (gurps-thaumatology#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: damage is modest at low mastery; dial: allow stronger attacks at higher levels, balanced by the required mastery or additional Realm.

rules.statement: A working using multiple Realms rolls once at the caster’s lowest relevant skill, with a -1 penalty for each Realm after the first. Its base energy cost is twice the highest Realm level involved, plus the levels of the other Realms; multiple Realms can broaden range or duration, enable transformations, and make the effect harder to counter.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Performing the Working; Energy Cost for Realm-Based Magic (gurps-thaumatology#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: combine Realms to achieve effects beyond one Realm; dial: each added Realm makes casting harder and increases energy use.
