rules.statement: For Realm-based enchantment, the lowest relevant Realm skill sets both the roll and the artifact’s Power. All involved skills must be at least 15 for normal or better mana, or 20 for low mana; energy cost is the sum of Realm levels used in the process multiplied by 150 if only a mage can use the item, or 250 if anyone can, counting a Realm again when it serves a separate role.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: bound Realm power can be made permanent in an artifact; dial: broad user access costs more energy, and low-mana operation demands higher skill.

rules.statement: A working’s energy cost can exceed the caster’s reserve: in the example, a 15-point casting costs 2 HP as well as energy. Its duration depends on margin of success in that setting, and maintaining the transformed boat costs half the casting cost—8 energy points per time increment; when the duration ends, the target returns to its prior form.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: duration and upkeep constrain costly transformations; dial: the setting determines duration increments and whether ongoing effects can be maintained.

rules.statement: Under the optional reactive-reality rule, workings accrue Distortion Points according to how unnatural they are and how they turn out: ordinary success on a standard working adds 1d-3 (minimum 0), failure adds 1, and critical failure adds 1d+1. When a gain brings the total to 3 or more, roll 3d; a result no greater than the total threatens a crisis, which may be resisted, and an unprevented crisis normally resets the total to zero while causing an additional consequence.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Errors and Side Effects: Reality Bites Back—Reactive Reality (gurps-thaumatology#021)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reactive reality is optional; dial: increase or reduce the distortion schedule to reflect how harshly the setting punishes unnatural magic.

rules.statement: A wizard can link a working to a future trigger so it remains inactive until a stated condition occurs. More Realms or Words in the link make its trigger more precisely defined but harder to cast; if the linked effect only partly works when triggered, an unpredictable result may follow.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: linked effects wait for a trigger; dial: precision raises casting difficulty and partial failure can produce strange outcomes.

rules.statement: Collaborators generally need identical or very similar syntactic systems. They may pool energy using ceremonial rules, or—when success margin matters—each participant able to perform the working rolls and adds their margin; any collaborator’s critical failure ruins the working and exposes everyone to the relevant critical-failure table, and any distortion gained by a participant is added to everyone’s total.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: coordinated casting can pool resources or improve the combined margin; dial: shared failure and shared distortion make collaboration risky.

rules.statement: An ancestry background can be priced at 5–10 points when it justifies one or two minor exceptional traits, but at 50–100 points when it enables a character to have a major supernatural advantage in a campaign of ordinary mortals; the GM may instead prohibit that concept. In a graded version, each nonhuman great-grandparent costs 10 points and allows one exotic or supernatural advantage, while 80 points can allow eight such advantages; especially major traits may require multiple grades.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Unusual Background (Supernatural Ancestry), pp. 198–199 (gurps-thaumatology#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modest ancestry benefits; dial up cost or prohibit access when the campaign assumes mortal-level characters, reflecting how exceptional the bloodline is.

rules.statement: Summonable Allies can bring in a replacement for a slain being, but the summoner must wait a full day before trying again. When the beings are essentially interchangeable and have no continuing memory or loyalty, the GM checks their willingness to follow orders each time they appear; this version costs +100%, whether or not replacements are possible.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a one-day gap and uncertain obedience; dial this when interchangeable summoned help is easy to replace but lacks an established bond.

rules.statement: A supernatural Talent can substitute for Magery as a prerequisite for enchantment spells only if the enchanter has at least two levels of the relevant Talent; the GM chooses eligible spells, and enchantments should generally improve an item's ordinary function rather than give it a wholly new magical capability. One assistant per Talent level can help if each has the appropriate craft skill at 15+ and participates in the required ritual; a Quick Gadgeteer may attempt Quick and Dirty enchantment, but cannot use Powerstones for it.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Enchantment Through Talent, pp. 198–200 (gurps-thaumatology#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to slow, craft-focused enchantment; dial toward faster work with skilled helpers, while limiting the result to the artifact's existing purpose.

rules.statement: A required behavioral disadvantage reduces a power modifier by 1% per disadvantage point. If breaking the requirement suspends power, add 5% when it fades gradually and subtract 5% when it changes rapidly and turns against the user; restoration that takes about a day adds 5%, while a week-scale remedy has no adjustment and a month-scale remedy subtracts 5%. If the resulting modifier is positive, treat it as 0%.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Calculating the Power Modifier, p. 203 (gurps-thaumatology#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the stated disadvantage and recovery adjustments; dial severity according to how quickly the source withdraws power and how costly repentance is.

rules.statement: A power drawing on a generally available external energy source takes a -5% modifier; if that source is relatively easy to cut off, use -10% instead. For mana, no-mana conditions prevent use, low mana imposes -5 on relevant rolls, and very high or wild mana may cause unusual behavior.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Calculating the Power Modifier, p. 203 (gurps-thaumatology#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a modest energy-source limitation; dial it harsher when the source can readily be denied, since users depend on the surrounding conditions.

rules.statement: Power Talent adds its level to rolls to activate or use abilities belonging to its power, including movement, attack, and mental-use rolls, but not to effect rolls, resistance rolls, or rolls required by limitations. Each ability belongs to one power, so a roll cannot receive bonuses from multiple Talents; a multi-roll ability can receive the appropriate Talent bonus on each roll.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to one Talent per ability and no stacking; dial breadth and price to prevent a broad supernatural Talent from outcompeting other sources of expertise.

rules.statement: When a magical ability is opposed by a spell that suppresses or negates it, the user usually rolls HT plus Talent for a physical ability or Will plus Talent for a mental ability in a Quick Contest. A spell that counters a specific ability generally requires the countering character to possess that ability, or one the GM considers sufficiently similar.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Dispelling Magical Advantages, p. 204 (gurps-thaumatology#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an opposed resistance and a requirement for a matching counter; dial similarity broadly or narrowly according to how specialized counter-magic is in the setting.

rules.statement: If an instantaneous spell shuts down a continuous magical ability, the user must spend a Ready maneuver and succeed at HT plus Talent for a physical ability, or Will plus Talent for a mental one, to restart it.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Dispelling Magical Advantages, p. 204 (gurps-thaumatology#022)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to an action and a successful recovery roll; dial how difficult it is to restore an ability after it has been suppressed.

rules.statement: An ability limited by Glamour changes living observers' perceptions through mental influence, not machines; each living observer can resist with Will, adding Mind Shield levels, and on success perceives the user normally. The resistance target determines the limitation value, from -5% at Will-5 to -50% at Will+4.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a resistible effect that does not fool machines; dial the Will target to represent how easily observers can see through the perception trick.

rules.statement: A long-lasting effect on another person can have a simple condition that ends it, such as speaking specified words or performing an act. The limitation is worth -5%, -10%, or -20% depending on whether the condition needs research, can be discovered by a skill roll, or is common knowledge; if it is hard to arrange even when known, each value improves by 5 percentage points.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the ordinary duration unless the target meets the stated release condition; dial the discount by how discoverable and achievable that condition is.

rules.statement: A power that reaches parallel worlds uses the distance as though both parties were on the same world. The enhancement costs +50% if it works only on other worlds or planes, or +100% if it also works in the user's current realm; the GM decides which abilities can use it.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to cross-world reach only; dial to +100% when the ability also works locally, reflecting the broader scope it provides.

rules.statement: A shamanic power can require ritual observance or a relationship with a patron spirit; if spirits are offended, they may oppose the shaman at a bad moment, but a modest sacrifice or roughly a day of prayer can usually appease them. Unreliable spirit-based powers may also fail because whimsical spirits or intermediaries are fickle.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a code of service and possible withdrawal; dial: make spirits more or less fickle or easier to appease; the shaman risks losing aid.

rules.statement: Shamanic Talent costs 5 points per level and adds to Will rolls to resist spiritual possession, including while using Channeling. A suitable form of Magery may substitute when it represents influence over spirits.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: trained resistance to possession; dial: allow a thematically matched substitute; the cost is investment in the relevant talent.

rules.statement: A soothsayer’s power may require ritual discipline (-5%), sustained contemplation (-10%), or near-detachment from ordinary life (-15%); a god-given version may instead demand a code of conduct. Power can be withdrawn quickly without danger, while restoration generally calls only for a minor quest or moderate sacrifice.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: guidance entails a prescribed way of life; dial: choose the severity and form of discipline; the soothsayer pays through restrictions and possible service to a higher power.

rules.statement: In a folkloric game, the GM may let magical NPCs act outside player-facing mechanics, while giving player characters narrowly specified gifts or one-use rituals. A ritual works only when its instructions are followed and may be limited to a particular time and place.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Freeform Folkloric Magic, p. 208 (gurps-thaumatology#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: effects are specific and story-controlled; dial: broaden a gift’s conditions or repeatability; the cost is dependence on exact instructions, circumstances, and GM adjudication.

rules.statement: A magician may gain apparent effects by summoning spirits, finding them through rumors or supernatural senses, or recruiting them through spirits already in service. Control can come from spells, rituals, a spirit’s binding rules or vulnerabilities, a usable key, or negotiated payment and influence.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Summoning and Binding, pp. 209-210 (gurps-thaumatology#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: servants must first be located and then controlled or persuaded; dial: make recruitment and control easier or more specialized; the cost is time, knowledge, leverage, or fair payment.

rules.statement: A spirit vessel uses a standard form supplied by the empowering entity, rather than choosing an arbitrary bundle of gifts; the GM defines the template and may reject concepts without a coherent link to that spirit. A vessel may use only the part of the template not already duplicated by personal traits.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Game Mechanics, p. 211; Templates and Personal Abilities, pp. 212-213 (gurps-thaumatology#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the patron’s nature determines the granted package; dial: permit only fitting partial templates; the vessel gives up selecting or freely customizing gifts.

rules.statement: Spirit-vessel templates commonly impose mental disadvantages reflecting the spirit’s intense personality, and these may have poor self-control values; possession can also impose physical or supernatural drawbacks. The spirit’s traits and code may strongly shape the host while empowered.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Disadvantages, p. 213; Limiting the Advantage, p. 214 (gurps-thaumatology#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: borrowed power carries the spirit’s temperament; dial: vary how severe or controlling those traits are; the host risks altered behavior and unwanted consequences.

rules.statement: A vessel who remains empowered can lose 1 FP per minute after the first minute, stopping the loss after one minute back in natural form; a less taxing version begins after an hour and costs 1 FP per 10 minutes, stopping after 10 minutes natural. Transforming itself can separately cost FP.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Exhausting Transformations, p. 213; Limiting the Advantage, p. 214 (gurps-thaumatology#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: extended empowerment strains the host; dial: set the onset and recovery intervals; the cost is fatigue spent while remaining in the borrowed state.

rules.statement: When personal and template traits conflict, disadvantages generally override advantages, while template traits usually supersede conflicting personal traits of the same kind. Compatible leveled traits add together without normal level caps, and disadvantage self-control values worsen according to their combined point value.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Templates and Personal Abilities, pp. 212-213 (gurps-thaumatology#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the spirit’s package controls conflicts and compatible traits stack; dial: the GM may remove irrelevant traits and adjust the form’s cost; the mortal may lose personal benefits or face intensified drawbacks.

rules.statement: A spirit may refuse or unpredictably grant a vessel’s transformation, impose rules through a pact, or take direct control in unexpected or stressful situations. A spirit that is dependable only in genuine danger can instead be limited to emergencies.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Limiting the Advantage, p. 214 (gurps-thaumatology#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reliability and control depend on the spirit’s disposition and conditions; dial: choose negotiation, rules, danger-only aid, or direct control; the cost is uncertainty or surrendered autonomy.

rules.statement: What a supernatural being grants can be withdrawn, and a GM enforcing the grantor’s code should veto uses that violate it; otherwise the reduced cost for the power is not justified. The GM should avoid withdrawing aid at a climactic moment merely to punish a breach if doing so would derail play.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: “The Lord Gave, and the Lord Hath Taken Away,” p. 211 (gurps-thaumatology#023)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: supernatural aid remains conditional on the grantor’s rules; dial: calibrate enforcement and chances to make amends; the user risks withdrawal, while excessive punishment can disrupt the game.

rules.statement: When a transformed object or being is undamaged, an appropriate new effect can restore its original form without harm. If it has been injured, restoration is still often possible, but its original form returns with a proportional degree of injury.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: restore the prior form; dial: allow restoration after damage, with proportional injury as the cost.

rules.statement: When one magical effect opposes another, first identify what the attack affects and what the defense protects against; a defense only applies when those targets overlap. A defense can then operate as a guard, screen, barrier, damper, or drain.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: resolve opposition by the effects’ actual targets and operation; dial: permit broader interactions, at the cost of less distinct magical systems.

rules.statement: A guard gives a new or improved resistance roll against an effect, and may force a resistance roll where none would normally apply. A guard that stops an effect outright can still be overcome, commonly through a Quick Contest.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: guards add resistance or stop specified effects; dial: make an absolute stop, at the cost of allowing an appropriate contest to overcome it.

rules.statement: When a guard requires an attacker to roll, the GM assigns a suitable skill or attribute roll; even an attack normally treated as automatic must receive a roll, set at 20 or the appropriate attribute or skill (including bonuses), whichever is higher. If a guard forces resistance against an attack that normally has none, the Rule of 16 does not apply, and the attack does not fail merely because the guard-required roll fails—the guard must successfully resist it.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a guard must successfully oppose the attack; dial: allow guards to introduce rolls even against normally automatic effects, at the cost of resolving the added defense.

rules.statement: Against an effect formed first and then used to attack, a guard usually contests the skill that created the effect in an attempt to disrupt its magical structure. A guard that deflects incoming energy instead contests the attack roll.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: disrupt creation or deflect the launched attack, according to the defense; dial: let a guard affect either stage when its operation justifies it.

rules.statement: A screen protects against effects needing activation or targeting by imposing a penalty on the attacker’s roll. If the attack normally requires no roll, the GM assigns one using the guidelines for guards.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: screens hinder attempts to activate or target an effect; dial: extend the penalty to all magic worked in a defined space, at the cost of maintaining the screen.

rules.statement: A barrier absorbs damage using a DR rating, normally ordinary DR, so armor divisors can penetrate it more effectively; some magic can provide DR that counts as Hardened. A barrier not attached to someone can also block movement, may be broken down, and may be instantly restored if a continuous supply of magical energy is available.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the barrier absorbs damage and may block passage; dial: make it Hardened or instantly renewable, at the cost of magical energy for renewal.

rules.statement: A damper reduces another effect’s power, such as an attribute, attack dice, or purchased levels. If necessary, reduce numeric effect values in proportion to the part of the effect’s character-point value removed; for a primarily resistible attack, each 10% reduction (round up) gives +1 to resistance rolls.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: reduce the target power in proportion to the amount damped; dial: apply damping to additional numeric values, at the cost of reducing the effect’s output.

rules.statement: A drain depletes energy, usually FP, rather than directly reducing an effect’s rated power. It can also sap energy from an incoming attack quickly enough to weaken that attack; estimate its FP cost, ignoring reductions such as skill-based cost reductions, and reduce damage or effectiveness in proportion.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: drains reduce energy and may weaken an incoming attack; dial: allow precise, fast draining, at the cost of energy taken from the target.

rules.statement: A drain defense removes energy from an incoming attack, and the attack’s strength falls in proportion to the energy removed. In the example, removing 3 of the 6 energy points associated with a 3d explosive fireball reduces it to 2d-2.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the reduction tracks the fraction of energy drained; dial: the GM may choose how the attack’s game statistics reflect that loss.

rules.statement: When opposed effects do not fit an attack-versus-defense procedure, resolve them with a Quick Contest, or a Regular Contest for a substantial, extended struggle. Choose relevant skills or attributes, and apply suitable bonuses for power and range modifiers for each contestant.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a Quick Contest handles ordinary struggles; dial: use a Regular Contest when the struggle is substantial.

rules.statement: A lengthy, effortful curse announcement can weaken a target’s resistance to one later magical attack of the announced general type: contest the caster’s Intimidation against the target’s Will plus Fearlessness, and apply the caster’s victory margin as a resistance penalty. If the target wins, it instead gains a bonus equal to half its victory margin, rounded down and capped at +5; only the most recent attempt applies, and both penalties and bonuses decline by 1 per two full days before the attack arrives.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: p. 228, Undermining Defenses With Fear (gurps-thaumatology#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the tactic can help or backfire and fades over time; dial: the GM decides which resistible attacks qualify and what circumstances grant modifiers.

rules.statement: A point of raw magic can be spent as an energy source to supply 5 energy points for a process that normally costs fatigue, or as a conductor to give +3 to one spellcasting or ritual skill roll. In enchantment, each point can instead count as 100 energy points.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: p. 227, Using Raw Magic (gurps-thaumatology#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each use consumes raw magic; dial: a setting can allow or disallow particular uses and thereby control the resource’s versatility.

rules.statement: Raw magic can be stored within a character as intangible energy bound to the soul or aura, at 1 point per advantage level; the store begins full. It normally cannot be taken, though the GM may permit theft through a potent, likely painful magical effect.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: p. 228, New Advantage: Raw Magic Store (gurps-thaumatology#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: capacity is limited by advantage level and stored energy is secure; dial: theft may be permitted, at the cost of a potent and painful effect.

rules.statement: Raw magic can be gathered from a place of power according to its richness and possibly the gatherer’s skill. Extracting it from the cosmic background is an alternative that takes hours, days, or weeks and yields about one-fifth of the skill roll’s success margin in points, rounded down.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: p. 227, The Stuff of Raw Magic (gurps-thaumatology#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: supplies are scarce and background extraction is slow with a low yield; dial: the GM sets a location’s richness and whether background extraction is possible.

rules.statement: Raw magic can have distinct flavors, and a character can use flavored material only to benefit the related type of magic. Morally flavored raw magic can influence the resulting magic; its nature may be harmful, and it may serve as a temptation offered by demons.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: a flavor restricts use to a related magical field; dial: the GM determines whether neutral or morally flavored varieties exist and what influence they have.

rules.statement: A spell that processes raw magic costs 1 energy per 5 points manipulated, rounded up. It can move stored raw magic into the caster’s own store up to capacity, or make minor changes to material raw magic so it is easier to transport, but cannot work on intangible raw magic held by someone else.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: p. 230, New Spell: Process Raw Magic (gurps-thaumatology#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: manipulation costs energy and is limited by the caster’s storage capacity; dial: the GM determines what counts as a minor transport-oriented change.

rules.statement: An insubstantial being can use abilities resisted by IQ, Will, or Per to affect substantial targets at -3; effects with no resistance roll can generally be used without that penalty, unless they have an offensive use, in which case they count as resisted. An ability specifically enhanced to affect substantial targets can cross without the penalty.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: p. 229, Insubstantial Beings Affecting the Material World (gurps-thaumatology#025)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: crossing the boundary incurs -3 for mentally resisted effects; dial: the GM may make an insubstantiality effect easier if its subject cannot affect substantial targets.

rules.statement: The five local magical domains each have four ranks: the first detects and assesses, the second gives minor command, the third permits minor creation, and the fourth allows total command. Each rank costs 15 points; the system excludes magic over minds, spirits, and souls, and healing cannot exceed natural processes, though it can speed them up.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: rank sets a domain’s scope, while explicit exclusions bound what magic can do; dial: the GM defines domains and their coverage.

rules.statement: Spirit-sensitive people can communicate with reachable spirits for generally useful but vague guidance; some can also uncover secrets or enter another person’s dreams, and a small number have powerful mental abilities.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Spiritualism and Ritual, p. 237 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: spiritual sensitivity permits contact and limited mental access; dial: make dream entry or secret-finding more consequential because spirits and targets may be evasive.

rules.statement: Trained adepts with Magery 0 can use Effect Shaping Path/Book magic, while non-mages may attempt it at -5; the broadly known Paths are Dreams, Knowledge, and Spirit. Path/Book Adept and higher Magery levels are unavailable, and mana level does not matter.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Spiritualism and Ritual, p. 237 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: training grants a narrow ritual practice and non-mages face a -5 penalty; dial: broaden access or the known Paths if occult learning is more common.

rules.statement: High Science users must take a vegetarian vow and need abundant living vegetation nearby or physical contact with vegetation within the last hour; otherwise their power becomes useless. Their power has a -10% modifier, divided between the vow and this vegetation-dependent energy source.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The High Science of Atlantis, pp. 237-238 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the vow and nearby living plant energy restrict use; dial: relax either condition at the cost of weakening the setting’s distinctive limits.

rules.statement: Modern users’ Mind Reading, Telesend, and Telekinesis are unreliable, activating on 11; Telekinesis is available up to level 8. Atlantean Weird Science is capped at 2 points, and specified skill thresholds permit lightweight materials or telekinetic force-beam weapons.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: The High Science of Atlantis, p. 238 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: an activation threshold of 11 and strict skill and level caps keep poorly understood powers erratic and specialized; dial: raise reliability or caps as Atlantean knowledge improves.

rules.statement: Spiritualist, Theosophist, and Atlantean effects interact readily, but no human action can compel or control older, stronger spirits: they bypass known wards and cannot be harmed by mortal energies. Summoning or commanding them is therefore impossible.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: shared spiritual forces allow interaction among human workings, while greater spirits resist mortal control and harm; dial: permit limited influence only if the hierarchy of being is meant to be less absolute.

rules.statement: A gem-injection user can access only the college associated with the gem currently used and cannot combine gems; switching while the previous dose remains active requires a HT-3 roll or unconsciousness for 3d minutes, and even success causes mental stunning. A dose enables magic for 2d×3 minutes, and spells can still be maintained after the dose’s effect ends.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Gem Injection Rules—Magery (Gem Injection), p. 241 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: each gem fixes the available college, and changing it during an active dose risks unconsciousness and stun; dial: ease switching if the intended play is less constrained by addiction and incompatible effects.

rules.statement: Gem-injection magic requires addiction and a fresh gem-drug dose to activate; users normally pay spell energy with FP but may instead spend HP. A critical failure uses the reality-warping results, except a result of 18 causes a heart attack.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Gem Injection Rules, p. 241 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: addiction, costly doses, possible HP expenditure, and severe failure consequences make the power dangerous; dial: reduce bodily risk or addiction pressure if the campaign needs less self-destruction.

rules.statement: Gem type determines which spells or colleges the user can access, with lists varying by gem; for example, jet grants Knowledge except for spells assigned to amethyst, plus Mind-Reading and Mind-Search. Ruby grants Fire and listed destructive spells, while also causing an obsession with justice and a refusal to willingly harm people the user considers innocent.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Gemstones and Their Effects, pp. 241-242 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: the consumed gem selects a bounded spell set, and ruby adds a moral fixation; dial: change the gem-to-spell mapping or the intensity of the fixation to suit the campaign.

rules.statement: Spell duration can be priced by duration bands: momentary is modifier 0, up to 10 minutes is 1, up to an hour is 2, up to a day is 4, up to a year is 9, and each doubling beyond a year adds 1. Alternatively, effects can end when a stated condition occurs, with its modifier based on how likely and soon that condition is to happen.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Variant Durations: Conditional Termination; Duration Effect Modifiers Table, pp. 242-243 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: longer-lasting effects require higher modifiers, while conditional endings are priced by likelihood; dial: adjust bands or condition estimates to fit the setting’s magic economy.

rules.statement: A line of ash can disrupt magic crossing it at -1 to -3, or give +1 to magic worked wholly inside an insulating circle. Iron can impose penalties as severe as -5 on or into protected targets and -7 on or across iron; it cannot insulate, and iron meant to contain magical power must first be magically neutralized.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Traditional Materials—Ashes and Iron, p. 245 (gurps-thaumatology#026)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default: ash and iron interfere with workings in different ways, and iron resists magical containment; dial: choose whether these material correspondences are universal or tradition-specific.

rules.statement: When a setting recognizes True Names, using the target’s identifier gives a bonus of +0 for a public name or pseudonym, +1 for a full legal name or identifying number, +2 for a private or secret name, +3 for an exceptionally unique identifier at the GM’s option, and +4 for a True Name. Use only the best available name bonus; the GM may allow a True Name to give more or ensure success for magic that calls a subject, and possibly for highly personal magic.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed best-identifier bonus; dial up for subject-calling magic, because the universe recognizes the True Name as uniquely identifying its subject.

rules.statement: Changing a True Name may require religious justification, legal work, destruction of original records, or convincing close relations to adopt and think of the new name. A successful change can take weeks, months, or years, with the old-name bonus fading as the new-name bonus grows; a replaced birth-name may remain a secret name worth +2 unless the ceremony severs its link.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Appendix, True Name Changes (gurps-thaumatology#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a slow, difficult transition; dial toward an impossible change when the universe cannot be persuaded to recognize a replacement.

rules.statement: Using a subject’s name or number is not required to target them, but a public name or clear informal identifier can still let magic locate them without a bonus. A unique identifier such as a complete DNA sequence may be worth +3 if it is not also being used as a sympathetic link.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to allowing an informal identifier to find a subject without improving the roll; dial up its bonus only when it uniquely identifies that person.

rules.statement: A magical link made from an item that has been in close contact with a target can grant a bonus: a personally important item gives +1, body material from a living subject or a physical piece of an inanimate target gives +2, and blood, semen, a corpse, or an equivalent substance gives +3. A physically present, unresisting child or spouse can also give +3; use only the best bonus, and do not combine this method with Sympathy on the same item.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to the listed best link bonus; dial down if the item is not genuinely personal, because an unmissed possession is a weak connection.

rules.statement: Minor contagious links are normally consumed when used, while substantial items can usually be reused but may lose potency over time. A caster can use personal material to claim a bonus when working magic on themselves, but possession of such material creates a risk if enemies capture it.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to consuming minor links and allowing substantial links repeated use; dial down their remaining potency over time as magic wears them out.

rules.statement: A sacrifice can add a skill bonus: food, drink, tobacco, stimulants, or incense gives +1 or +2; valuable goods give +1 to +3; live animals give +2 to +4; and human sacrifices, if acceptable, give +1 to +5. A supernatural example of a category adds +1 beyond its highest listed bonus; the GM may cap total sacrifice bonuses at +6.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to bonuses based on symbolic value and quality, capped at +6; dial higher only for a sacrifice-intensive game, because offerings must be notably valuable or resonant.

rules.statement: Bonuses from multiple sacrifices can add together, except food and animal offerings do not stack: use whichever of those two has the higher bonus. A sacrifice must belong to the caster or be fully under their control, and killing an enemy in battle does not count; the same magical ingredient cannot grant both a sacrifice bonus and another bonus at once.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to limited stacking and require control of the offering; dial down when the same ingredient is being claimed under another magical principle.

rules.statement: A sacrifice that violates a divine or metaphysical principle can impose a penalty at least twice the size of its listed bonus. In settings where spirits reject human sacrifice, it may attract only spirits or energies associated with harm and negative emotions; a willing human sacrifice may instead earn a bonus where the relevant spirits accept it.
locators: GURPS Thaumatology: Appendix, Sacrifice Bonuses; Complications (gurps-thaumatology#027)
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to a penalty at least double the listed bonus for a violation; dial toward acceptance or rejection according to the spirits’ principles.

rules.statement: A caster may be able to use their own injury as an offering, gaining +1 for each full 20% of their HP spent. If a Will roll succeeds exactly, the expenditure works but the first roll for the magic takes a shock penalty appropriate to the HP spent; failure on a required skill roll can cause a few HP of real injury, and a later HT failure may leave permanent scars or other lasting effects.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to +1 per full 20% HP paid and a possible shock penalty; dial toward lasting harm when the ritual is disastrous or invokes dangerous forces.

rules.statement: The date or season can modify particular magic: national-day workings for a nation’s interests may gain +1 to +3, May Day workings for new beginnings or radical change may gain +1 to +3, and Guy Fawkes Night explosion magic may gain +1 or +2. Equinoxes and solstices can give +1 or +2 to some temporary effects but impose -3 or worse on attempts to make effects permanent; the GM may assign other bonuses or penalties to festivals and culturally significant dates.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to modifiers tied to the working’s association with the date; dial by culture and calendar, because a date’s significance depends on shared or astronomical meaning.

rules.statement: A mystic who enters a spiritual sphere in the proper sequence may qualify for bonuses to related magic or for aspected magical ability. Entry out of sequence or without ritual preparation can cause severe consequences, and access may be required to use particular magical verbs in some settings.
rules.speaker: rulebook
rules.default_dial_reason: Default to requiring correct order and preparation; dial toward broader access only where mystical insight is not a prerequisite for magical power.
